items.title: ‘Poets only sell books from car boots’ – Nana Asaase recounts disrespect in his poetry journey
items.description: Ghanaian poet and writer Nana Asaase has opened up about the dismissive comments he faced when he started his poetry career, including claims that poets and writers in Ghana could only make a living selling books from car boots. Speaking on The Career Trail programme aired on Joy Learning TV and Joy News, Nana Asaase recounted how such remarks made him question his decision to pursue poetry. “Someone once told me poets and Ghanaian writers, all they do is sell books in a car boot,” he recalled. According to the poet, the comments were discouraging, but his conviction that he was on the right path kept him going. “Sometimes when things get tough, I look into the mirror and think, why not just quit poetry and join my family business? Because we had a bakery. But something within me kept telling me I was on the right path. I shouldn’t give up, so I kept pushing,” he shared. After 12 years in poetry, Nana Asaase says his persistence has gradually paid off, with his work opening doors to opportunities he never imagined when he started. “This same job people looked down on me when I started has given me great opportunities. I have performed for presidents. All four presidents of this Fourth Republic, dead or alive, have been my audience,” he revealed. “Sometimes, somebody shows up, you don’t know the person from anywhere and says, ‘Oh, I know this young man. Give this job to him.’ You do a fantastic job, meanwhile, I have not met this person,” he continued. Nana Asaase attributed his perseverance to his faith in God, saying his relationship with God remained the foundation of his journey. “Once you know your source, make sure you’re at peace with your source. Mine is God. I have no shady dealings backing me,” he noted. He also highlighted discipline and consistency as important to developing and sustaining a career in poetry. “There’s no magic. Practice, practice, practice. As I’m sitting here, I’m practicing. When I drive, I practice. When I eat, I practice. When I have conversations, I practice,” he said. After 12 years in poetry, Nana Asaase is preparing to release his first book this year. “By God’s grace, I’m releasing my first book this year, and I will not sell my book out of a car boot. My books will be sold all over the world on very prominent counters,” he disclosed with excitement. And having experienced the challenges of building a career in poetry, Nana Asaase is also using his Sankofa Sessions, which include the Mental Pictures initiative, to nurture other talents and encourage a greater appreciation for literary arts, storytelling, oratory and self-expression.

items.title: JUSAG threatens indefinite strike from November 2 over unpaid salary review
items.description: The Judicial Service Staff Association of Ghana (JUSAG) has threatened an indefinite strike from Monday, November 2, 2026, if the government fails to approve its 2026 salary review and pay outstanding arrears. The association has given the government until Sunday, November 1, to meet its demands, warning that its members will withdraw their services until the issues are resolved. In a notification letter dated October 23 and signed by its General Secretary, Abdulai Yakubu, JUSAG informed the National Labour Commission (NLC) of its intention to embark on the industrial action over delays in reviewing salaries and related allowances for Judicial Service staff. The association said the conditions of service of its members are governed by Article 149 of the 1992 Constitution and the Judicial Service (Terms and Conditions of Service) Regulations, 2025 (C.I. 141). According to JUSAG, it requested a review of salaries for 2026 after the previous salary review expired in December 2025. The Judicial Council subsequently completed its work and submitted its recommendations to the President in accordance with Article 149 of the Constitution and Regulation 25 of C.I. 141. However, JUSAG said the approval process had stalled despite repeated appeals for action. “Owing to the delay in concluding the process, JUSAG, by a letter dated 19th January 2026, wrote to the Judicial Council to expedite the process. However, little progress resulted,” the notification stated. The association said it again reminded management of the matter in a letter dated September 10, 2026. It also cited appeals made during the 2nd Quadrennial Delegates’ Conference in Tamale, the 45th Association of Magistrates and Judges of Ghana (AMJG) Conference in Accra, and the Chief Justice’s Staff Durbar in Tamale. JUSAG said the appeals had produced assurances but no concrete action towards approving the Judicial Council’s recommendations and paying the revised salaries. The association said the delay had heightened tensions and weakened staff morale, particularly because other public sector workers had received approval and payment of their revised 2026 salaries in January. “We are now in the tenth month of the year, and our members are still waiting—patiently, but no longer quietly. This situation has heightened tension and dampened morale among staff of the Judicial Service,” the letter stated. JUSAG also expressed concern that negotiations by Organised Labour over the 2027 base pay were already underway while its members were still waiting for their revised 2026 salaries and allowances. JUSAG’s National Executive Council has set out two conditions for calling off the planned industrial action. The association wants the government to: Approve the Judicial Council’s recommendations on the 2026 salary review by October 31, 2026. Pay the revised salaries in November, including arrears covering January to October 2026. The association said failure to meet the demands by November 1 would trigger an indefinite strike from the following day. It added that the strike would remain in force until the demands were met. JUSAG said it had repeatedly urged its members to exercise restraint because of the potential consequences of industrial action for justice delivery and national security. The planned strike could disrupt the administrative and support services of the Judicial Service if the government and the association fail to reach an agreement before the deadline. The notification letter was copied to the Office of the President, the Judicial Secretary, the Attorney-General and Minister for Justice, the Minister of Finance, and the Minister for Jobs, Labour and Employment Relations. items.title: Temwa Chawinga becomes first African woman to finish in Ballon d’Or top 10
items.description: Malawian forward Temwa Chawinga has made history by becoming the first African woman to finish in the top 10 of the women’s Ballon d’Or. Chawinga’s achievement marks a significant milestone for African women’s football, placing the Malawi international among the world’s leading female players. Born on September 20, 1998, in Rumphi District, Malawi, Chawinga plays as a forward for Kansas City Current and the Malawi national team. She has enjoyed considerable success at club level, winning four Chinese Women’s Super League titles with Wuhan Jianghan University in 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2023. She also won the NWSL x Liga MX Femenil Summer Cup in 2024 and the NWSL Shield in 2025 with Kansas City Current. Her individual honours include two consecutive NWSL Most Valuable Player awards in 2024 and 2025, as well as two NWSL Golden Boots in the same years. Chawinga also claimed the Chinese Women’s Super League Golden Boot in 2022 and 2023 before winning the International Federation of Football History and Statistics (IFFHS) World’s Best Top Goal Scorer award in 2023. She was joined in the Ballon d’Or top 10 by Haiti’s Melchie Dumornay, Norway’s Caroline Graham Hansen, Spain’s Patri Guijarro, Denmark’s Pernille Harder, Poland’s Ewa Pajor, Spain’s Clàudia Pina and Alexia Putellas, England’s Alessia Russo, and Jamaica’s Khadija Shaw. The list features players from Europe, Africa and the Caribbean, reflecting the growing global reach of women’s football. Chawinga’s historic finish represents a breakthrough for African representation in the prestigious individual award and further highlights her rise as one of the leading figures in the women’s game. items.title: Police confirm man, teenager swept away by flood in Aba
items.description: By Steve Oko Abia State Police Command has confirmed that a man who attempted to rescue a teenage girl from a water-filled ditch at Faulks Road, Aba, was swept away alongside the girl during Sunday’s downpour. The Police Public Relations Officer, Maureen Chinaka, disclosed this while responding to Vanguard inquiries, confirming that the incident occurred around the popular Ukwu Mango area of the commercial city. Chinaka said the tragedy happened near an ongoing construction site where an uncovered ditch had filled with rainwater. According to her, the teenage girl was passing through the area when she reportedly hit a stone and fell into the ditch. An adult who witnessed the incident reportedly plunged into the water in an attempt to rescue her, but both were swept away. “Unfortunately, we have not been able to see them. The police are aware, and the matter has been reported. Efforts are in place to see how they can be rescued,” Chinaka said. She confirmed that the two victims had yet to be found as search efforts continued. Asked whether the construction company responsible for the site would face possible charges over negligence, the police spokesperson said investigations were ongoing. The tragedy has raised concerns about the safety of construction sites during heavy rainfall, particularly where excavations and drainage channels are left uncovered and become submerged in floodwater. Aba’s flat terrain makes parts of the commercial city vulnerable to flooding during heavy downpours, increasing the risks posed by waterlogged roads, open drains and excavations. The post Police confirm man, teenager swept away by flood in Aba appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Unregistered Airbnb operators in Kasoa face prosecution as GTA intensifies enforcement
items.description: The Ghana Tourism Authority (GTA) has shut down several unregistered accommodation facilities in Kasoa and surrounding areas for operating without the required licences. The Authority said the operators had repeatedly been notified to register their facilities in accordance with the Registration and Licensing of Food, Beverage and Entertainment Enterprises, 2016 (L.I. 2238), but failed to comply. During the enforcement exercise, the Accra West Regional Director of the GTA, Richard Agyenim Boateng, said operating an accommodation facility without the required registration and licence was illegal. He warned that operators who reopen their facilities without meeting the necessary requirements could face prosecution. Mr Boateng explained that the exercise was intended to enforce tourism regulations while helping to protect the safety and satisfaction of guests. “We are mandated to close down all facilities that are not registered. These facilities have failed to register with us and have ignored our notices. That is why we are here to ensure they do the right thing. They operate Airbnb facilities, and we want them to come to our office to go through the registration process and obtain licences,” he told Accra-based Citi FM. The GTA is urging operators of accommodation facilities, including Airbnb properties, to visit its offices and complete the registration and licensing process to ensure compliance with the law. The enforcement exercise forms part of the Authority’s efforts to ensure that tourism-related businesses operate within the required regulatory framework.

items.title: Impunity, justice system failure fuelling violence in North Central — Osinbajo
items.description: By Golok Nanmwa Former Vice President of Nigeria, Prof. Yemi Osinbajo, has attributed the widespread insecurity in North Central Nigeria and other parts of the country to failures in the justice system and inadequate punitive measures for crimes committed. Osinbajo stated this on Monday in Plateau State at a forum titled, “Countering Polarisation and Rebuilding Civic Cohesion in North Central Nigeria Beyond Tribe and Faith, Reclaiming Our Shared Stories,” organised by Justice Research Institute, JRI, in partnership with the National Institute for Policy and Strategic Studies, NIPSS. The former Vice President said, “Impunity destroys the fabric of society. There must be clear and enforceable consequences for wrongdoing and offences committed against the state or individuals.” “If there are no consequences for actions taken under any guise, there will be no way to rebuild and reconcile. Peace cannot be built without justice.” “Those who have been displaced and whose communities or villages have been illegally occupied must be returned to their ancestral homes. Victims must also be compensated.” “If you look at the land-grabbing situation, land must be returned to its rightful owners. “ “This is the process of rebuilding. There must be compensation, the proper procedure must be followed, and any wrongdoing must result in a penalty. “The problems of justice administration in Nigeria require urgent attention in the form of reforms to address the majority of the issues impeding justice delivery.” “It is better for the country to recognise that we have a system that requires immediate intervention.” “For peace to reign, we must reorient our attitudes towards ourselves and others, particularly our brothers and sisters. I believe we should return to the basics, and this should be done intentionally.” He added, “Reconciliation must be deliberate and genuine. Regardless of what happened in Rwanda, they are back together because leaders and governments made a deliberate and intentional effort to bring people together. “I believe there is a need for deliberate and intentional reconciliation and peace-building, which can only be accomplished by government in collaboration with civil society organisations and religious leaders. “Many of these will be determined by our country’s elite.” In his welcome address, the Director-General of NIPSS, Prof. Ayo Omotayo, said, “Storytelling is a powerful instrument for peace-building and national reconciliation. “Societies are held together not only by laws and institutions but also by the stories citizens tell about themselves and one another.” “Stories shape our memories, influence how we understand our differences and imagine our common future.” “They can inspire solidarity, but when distorted or manipulated, they can deepen grievances and turn neighbours into enemies.” Also speaking, the former Chief Justice and Emir of Lafia, Justice Sidi Bage, said, “Conflict often begins long before violence erupts. Conflict starts when justice, identity and belonging are denied.” “North Central Nigeria is a microcosm of the country’s diversity, and we must caution against narratives that exaggerate differences between indigenes and settlers, farmers and herders, or adherents of different faiths.” “Communication and active listening are indispensable for peaceful coexistence. “In the courtroom, a judge must listen to both sides before reaching a decision. In our communities, we must also be willing to hear perspectives that differ from our own.” He added, “If we are to rebuild trust and strengthen peaceful coexistence, we must create spaces where people can listen to one another, understand their differences and address grievances before they escalate into violence.” The post Impunity, justice system failure fuelling violence in North Central — Osinbajo appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Teacher trainee allowances: TTAG explains payment delays at three colleges, assures affected students
items.description: The Teacher Trainees’ Association of Ghana (TTAG) has attributed delays in the payment of allowances to students at three colleges of education to outstanding clearance requirements. According to the association, Savannah College of Education, Christ the Teacher College of Education and Ghana Muslim Mission College of Education have yet to receive the necessary clearance to facilitate payment. In a statement issued on Monday, October 26, TTAG said its leadership had engaged the Student Loan Trust Fund (SLTF) following complaints from trainees who did not receive their allowances during the recent disbursement. “It was identified that clearance had not been granted for Savannah College of Education, Christ the Teacher College of Education, and Ghana Muslim Mission College of Education,” the statement explained. The association further disclosed that trainees of Al-Faruq College of Education who missed the recent disbursement are expected to receive their allowances before the end of October 2026. TTAG consequently urged students across the country’s 49 public colleges of education to verify their registration details and Ghana Commercial Bank (GCB) account status to avoid further payment delays. “All trainees are encouraged to verify their registration details and Ghana Commercial Bank (GCB) account status and promptly rectify any errors or outstanding requirements to facilitate payment happening any moment from now,” the statement said. The association assured affected trainees that it would continue engaging the SLTF and other relevant stakeholders to resolve outstanding payment challenges. It reiterated its commitment to ensuring that all eligible trainees receive their allowances as soon as possible.

items.title: From KNUST to Yale: Ghanaian veterinarian makes history at Yale School of the Environment
items.description: Dr Daniel Baba Abiliba has become the first Ghana-trained veterinarian to enrol at the Yale School of the Environment (YSE). Dr Abiliba joined YSE’s Master of Environmental Management (MEM) programme in August 2026. He is also the first Ghanaian to receive the MSD Animal Health/World Veterinary Association (WVA) Veterinary Student Scholarship. “KNUST and its social environment gave me my foundation. Everything I bring to Yale, I learned first in Ghana, in our classrooms, on our farms and from our farmers,” Dr Abiliba remarked. Milestones and key achievements In 2018, while pursuing his studies at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Dr Abiliba received the MSD/WVA Veterinary Student Scholarship. The international scholarship recognises veterinary students who demonstrate outstanding leadership and dedication to the profession. “Receiving that scholarship reaffirmed that the work we are doing in Ghana has a place on the global stage. This inspired me to pursue greater ambitions, ultimately leading me to the Yale School of the Environment. It also instilled in me a sense of responsibility to pave the way for the next generation of students,” he said. He obtained his Doctor of Veterinary Medicine degree from the KNUST School of Veterinary Medicine in 2022. Veterinary science at the core of environmental sustainability At Yale, Dr Abiliba is studying the intersection of food systems, public health and the environment. His work draws on the One Health approach, which recognises that the health of people, animals and ecosystems is closely interconnected. “How we raise animals affects the land, the water and our own health. Veterinarians have an important role to play in environmental decision-making, and I want to help bring that perspective into the rooms where decisions are made,” he said. Before joining Yale, Dr Abiliba founded the Animal Welfare League (AWL), a non-profit organisation focused on improving farmed animal welfare in Ghana and across Africa. Inspiring the next generation of veterinarians Dr Abiliba hopes his journey will encourage Ghanaian veterinary students to explore broader career opportunities beyond traditional veterinary practice. “Veterinary medicine is not only about treating sick animals, it is about food security, disease prevention, and protecting the environment we all depend on. The next generation of Ghanaian vets can lead in all of these spaces,” Dr Abiliba said. He credits his family, particularly his parents, and his mentors at the KNUST School of Veterinary Medicine for supporting him throughout his journey.

items.title: Pezeshkian urges 'regional unity' in meeting with Makkah pact countries in Tehran
items.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Monday called for “regional unity” at a meeting in Tehran with representatives of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, which recently signed the Makkah defence pact. “I hope that the presence of representatives of important and influential Islamic countries at this meeting will help further consolidate regional unity and cohesion,” Pezeshkian said, according to a statement shared on the presidential website, urging Islamic countries to “stand together and adopt a coordinated position”. “Muslims are brothers to one another and must stand together as a united front against threats and actions targeting Muslim nations,” he stressed. Condemning Israel’s actions in Gaza and other regional countries, he said: “We must not allow the Israeli regime to assassinate and aggress against any individual or country whenever it desires. I am confident that if Islamic countries stand alongside each other and adopt a coordinated stance, the possibility of such actions repeating will not exist.” The Iranian president also criticised the United States for claiming “readiness for negotiation and dialogue simultaneously with attacking Iran” during the war. Pezeshkian stressed the need for translating political understandings into practical actions, stating: “We are determined to tread this path, but achieving this goal requires Islamic countries to reach a common understanding of their objectives, draw a clear vision, and pursue the implementation of agreements with mutual commitment until results are achieved.” He cautioned against policies of the United States and Israel that were aimed at “creating a rift among Muslim nations”, and called for heightened vigilance. The Iranian president also called for increased cooperation among regional countries in various fields. Iran’s IRIB state broadcaster earlier shared a video of the meeting, saying the quadrilateral meeting on “regional security and stability” had begun. The video showed Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi sitting with Iran’s president, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and security chief Mohsen Rezaei. Earlier in the day, Inter-Services Public Relations had confirmed that CDF Munir was visiting Tehran, but did not share any further details. The talks also included Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman and Turkiye’s intelligence chief, Ibrahim Kalin. At the start of the meeting, Iran’s state broadcaster reported the meeting was bringing together Iran, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye to discuss “regional cooperation, the US-Israeli aggression against Iran and its consequences”, among other topics. State-run PressTV also shared pictures of the meeting. Following the meeting, Rezaei, head of Supreme National Security Council, told state television, “Very good discussions took place between us.” “I feel that a new atmosphere is emerging in the region … I sensed a very positive atmosphere in the discussions among the gentlemen.” Iranian state television reported that the four countries agreed to continue talks after a “first” meeting in Tehran. It said they “agreed to continue discussions to strengthen cooperation… including on regional peace and security”. ‘Endogenous security’ Earlier, Iran’s state-run IRNA news agency quoted the deputy secretary of Iran’s top security body, Ali Bagheri Kani, as saying that the visit was part of efforts to implement the idea of endogenous security in West Asia. Iran’s foreign ministry spokesperson, Esmaeil Baqaei, said during a media briefing that the meeting with officials from the three countries would cover “most pressing issues threatening our region”, which included Israel’s expansionist policies, developments in Palestine and Lebanon. He added that the topic of “top priority on the agenda would be consequences of the US-Israeli aggression against Iran and its ramifications for the entire region”. IRNA further quoted him as saying that this meeting could be a prelude to further steps towards shaping “endogenous security — an issue that we have been insisting on for decades”. “We emphasise that regional security will not be ensured except by relying on the … security considerations of the countries of the region,” he said, adding that events of the last two years, especially the past eight months, had shown that sustainable and reliable security would only be made possible by “building trust and cooperation among the countries in the region”. Saudi Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly had also confirmed the visit in a post on X. Krimly described the visit as “part of the continued efforts by the Makkah Defence Alliance members for de-escalation between parties involved in the ongoing crisis, and promoting dialogue and diplomatic solutions, in support of the mediation efforts carried out by Qatar and Pakistan”. “The visit underscores the pivotal role of Makkah Defence Alliance members in reinforcing regional security and stability, and working with all countries in the region to achieve that goal,” he added. The visit comes as attacks by Houthis have spiralled over recent weeks and rhetoric between Washington and Tehran has grown more heated. Monday’s planned talks would be the first high-level contact between Iran and all members of the Makkah Defence Alliance since Saudi Arabia was drawn deeper into the conflict. Under the Makkah pact, signed in August, an armed attack on one member is considered an attack on all. CDF Munir had visited Iran last week. During the visit, Iranian leaders had conveyed that the US must take the first steps to rebuild trust, and that the acceptance of Tehran’s seven-point proposal could provide a starting point for renewed negotiations. According to Iran’s ISNA news agency, Baqaei said during the media briefing that the suggestion for the meeting was made during CDF Munir’s visit to Tehran last week. Tehran reviewed the proposal “favourably … and it is scheduled to be held today”, he added. War has engulfed the Middle East since late February when the US and Israel launched a wave of surprise attacks on Iran, just as Washington and Tehran were in the middle of negotiations on Iran’s nuclear programme. An April ceasefire brought an end to the initial phase of intense bombardment but the two sides have continued to vie for control of the Strait of Hormuz, through which around a fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas used to travel. Iran claims control over the strait and regularly targets vessels that attempt to cross without its authorisation, while the United States has imposed a naval counter-blockade on Iranian ports. Diplomatic efforts to resolve the crisis remain stalled, especially since the collapse of a June deal which laid out a pathway to a permanent settlement. The war has since spread across the region to include fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis in Yemen.

items.title: Aide sociale directe : Le PLF 2027 prépare une refonte du ciblage des bénéficiaires
items.description: Le projet de loi de finances (PLF) pour 2027 prévoit une nouvelle étape dans la réforme de l’aide sociale directe au Maroc. Au-delà de la revalorisation progressive du montant minimal de l’allocation mensuelle, qui doit passer de 500 à 1.000 dirhams, le gouvernement entend renforcer le fonctionnement du dispositif, affiner les critères d’éligibilité et améliorer l’accompagnement des ménages bénéficiaires. Une première hausse, portant le montant minimal à 600 dirhams, est prévue en 2027. Dans la note de présentation du PLF, l’exécutif présente l’année 2027 comme une étape de consolidation institutionnelle et opérationnelle du dispositif, après sa mise en œuvre progressive. Les priorités affichées portent sur une plus grande équité dans le ciblage des bénéficiaires et une amélioration de la qualité des services. L’ambition est également de faire évoluer progressivement l’aide sociale directe, aujourd’hui fondée sur des transferts monétaires, vers un instrument d’inclusion et d’autonomie économiques. Un ciblage davantage fondé sur les revenus réels L’un des principaux chantiers concerne les critères d’attribution des aides. Le gouvernement prévoit de préparer une transition progressive d’un système reposant principalement sur l’indice socio-économique vers un modèle tenant davantage compte du revenu réellement disponible des ménages. Cette évolution doit s’accompagner de la mise en place progressive d’une déclaration sociale globale des revenus et du renforcement des échanges sécurisés de données entre les administrations et les organismes concernés. Pendant la période transitoire, l’indice socio-économique sera conservé comme outil complémentaire lorsque les données disponibles sur les revenus ne seront pas suffisamment fiables. Le gouvernement prévoit également de renforcer les mécanismes d’actualisation de la situation des ménages, de recours et de rectification afin de réduire les erreurs d’inclusion et d’exclusion. Les revenus occasionnels ou saisonniers devront aussi être pris en considération. L’objectif est d’éviter qu’une variation temporaire des ressources entraîne automatiquement la perte du droit aux aides. Le transfert de la gestion à l’Agence nationale de soutien social Le gouvernement entend également achever le transfert de la gestion du dispositif à l’Agence nationale de soutien social. Le processus doit porter sur les fonctions actuellement assurées par la Caisse nationale de sécurité sociale (CNSS) et la Caisse nationale de retraite et d’assurance (CNRA), tout en garantissant la continuité des services destinés aux bénéficiaires. Cette réorganisation doit s’accompagner d’un renforcement des procédures, des capacités opérationnelles et des systèmes d’information liés au dispositif. Le transfert des systèmes d’information vers une infrastructure souveraine et moderne, exploitée par l’Agence nationale de soutien social, doit commencer en décembre 2026. Il s’agira également de consolider les mécanismes de sécurité, de continuité de service et de performance. Sur le terrain, le gouvernement mise sur une couverture territoriale plus étendue et une amélioration du traitement des demandes. La présence de l’agence doit notamment être renforcée après l’ouverture prévue de ses représentations à Sidi Kacem et à Taounate à la fin de 2026. Les dispositifs d’information, d’orientation et d’accompagnement des bénéficiaires seront eux aussi consolidés. En matière de traitement des réclamations et des recours, une modernisation progressive est annoncée pour 2027, avec le déploiement d’un assistant virtuel fondé sur l’intelligence artificielle. Celui-ci devra répondre aux questions les plus fréquemment posées. Une fonctionnalité de dépôt électronique des pièces justificatives est également prévue. Encourager l’emploi déclaré sans rompre la protection sociale L’autre volet de la réforme concerne l’accompagnement des ménages vers l’insertion professionnelle, sans remise en cause des droits acquis en matière de protection sociale. Parmi les mesures programmées figure la mise en place d’une prime exceptionnelle destinée à accompagner le chef de ménage ou l’un des deux conjoints lorsqu’il accède à un emploi déclaré dans le secteur privé. Cette mesure vise à encourager le recours à l’emploi déclaré. Le gouvernement prévoit également un mécanisme de rétablissement de l’éligibilité en cas de perte involontaire d’emploi, sans condition de durée minimale préalable de non-déclaration auprès de la CNSS. Il s’agit d’éviter les ruptures de protection sociale et de mieux prendre en compte l’évolution de la situation professionnelle des ménages. Le calendrier prévoit par ailleurs une deuxième revalorisation des montants mensuels des aides liées à l’enfance, conformément aux échéances fixées par le décret n° 2.23.1067. Le gouvernement entend poursuivre, parallèlement, l’amélioration du ciblage et le contrôle des conditions d’éligibilité. Des expérimentations dans la santé, l’éducation et l’emploi Enfin, des expérimentations territoriales doivent être conduites auprès des ménages bénéficiaires. Ces initiatives feront l’objet d’un suivi et d’une évaluation et porteront sur plusieurs domaines : la santé, la scolarisation et la facilitation de l’accès au marché du travail. À travers ces mesures, l’exécutif entend dépasser la seule logique de transfert financier pour renforcer les effets sociaux du dispositif et favoriser l’inclusion économique des ménages bénéficiaires. items.title: Mallam Junction traffic congestion hotspot cleared after JoyNews extensive report
items.description: After three years of torturous gridlock, missed opportunities and daily frustration, commuters who use the Mallam Junction stretch can finally breathe a sigh of relief. The notorious pothole-ridden section of the highway, which for years turned a short commute into a hours-long ordeal, has been fixed – just days after JoyNews shone a spotlight on the nightmare. For residents of Kasoa, Weija, Gbawe, Mallam and adjoining communities, Mallam Junction is more than just an intersection. It is the gateway to Accra for thousands travelling from the Central and Western Regions. But that gateway had become a trap. The trouble began three years ago when heavy rains devastated parts of Accra. The road at Mallam Junction was hard hit, leaving behind deep, yawning potholes that forced drivers to crawl, swerve, and sometimes stall completely. What should have been a smooth drive became a daily pain for commuters. During morning and evening rush hours, the situation was unbearable. Vehicles piled up bumper-to-bumper, engines overheated, tempers flared, and time stood still. On a typical Monday morning, the queue would stretch from Mallam Junction all the way to Broadcasting Junction at New Bortianor in the Ngleshie-Amanfro area. The human cost was enormous. Workers reported to the office late and queried by bosses. Traders lost valuable market hours. Students missed classes. Patients on their way to hospitals endured painful delays. To outsmart the traffic, many Kasoa residents say they were forced to adopt an extreme routine – leaving home as early as 4:00 a.m. just to beat the Mallam snarl and get to Accra on time. Those who could not wake that early had to accept being late as part of life. For three years, they pleaded. For three years, nothing changed – until JoyNews told their story. An extensive JoyNews report captured the depth of the suffering, with videos of gridlocked vehicles, interviews with stranded passengers, and drone shots of the deteriorating road. The report triggered public outrage and finally caught the attention of the authorities. Within days of the broadcast, machinery moved to site. The failed portion has now been patched and levelled, allowing for the free flow of traffic once again. Daniel Awortwe, Engineer at the Weija-Gbawe Municipal Assembly, and his team, who are carrying out the repair works confirmed that the repair works were executed through collaboration between the Municipal Assembly and the Ministry of Roads and Highways. According to him, the intervention was aimed at restoring the road to motorable condition and easing the unbearable congestion. Today, cars glide through Mallam Junction without the usual jerking and braking. Commercial drivers who once spent hours navigating a few metres now drive through in minutes. Commuters have welcomed the relief, though their joy is mixed with questions. Gladys Appiah, a regular passenger on the Kasoa-Accra route, could not hide her excitement. She expressed gratitude to the Minister of Roads and Highways, Kwame Agbodza, for acting swiftly after the JoyNews report. But for others like Yaa Serwaa, the celebration feels misplaced. She described the three-year delay as a self-inflicted wound. According to her, fixing potholes on a major international highway is not a capital-intensive project that requires huge loans or complex engineering. It is basic maintenance that should never have taken three years to fix. Her sentiment reflects a broader frustration among many Ghanaians – why must it take a media report for authorities to act on obvious problems? For now, however, the road is clear. The horns have reduced. The long queues have disappeared. And the 4:00 a.m. exodus from Kasoa may no longer be necessary, but the good news seems not good for hawkers who sell on the pavement during the traffic build-up. Akua says she makes GHC600.00 a day, but today she has been here for many hours with no sales. Whether this repair will be maintained to prevent another three-year ordeal remains to be seen.

items.title: El Niño: What it means and how Nigerians should prepare
items.description: By Sekinat Osundiji Nigeria may experience increased heat and changing rainfall patterns as a strengthening El Niño event raises concerns about its potential effects on agriculture, water supply, electricity generation and public health. The World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) said in September 2026 that El Niño was expected to strengthen into a very strong event and persist into early 2027. The Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet) has also warned that the phenomenon could affect rainfall patterns, including the length of the rainy season and when it ends. But what is El Niño, how could it affect Nigeria, and what can the country do to prepare? What is El Niño? El Niño is a natural climate phenomenon that occurs when surface waters in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean become warmer than average. This warming affects atmospheric circulation, changing weather patterns around the world. Depending on the region, it can contribute to higher temperatures, reduced or excessive rainfall, and shifts in seasonal conditions. El Niño is part of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), a climate pattern that also includes La Niña, its cooler phase, and neutral conditions. According to the WMO, El Niño typically occurs every two to seven years and lasts between nine and 12 months. Although it develops thousands of kilometres from Nigeria, its influence on global atmospheric circulation can affect weather in West Africa. However, its effects vary by location and do not automatically mean drought or extreme heat everywhere. What does El Niño mean for Nigeria? NiMet’s August 2026 seasonal climate update identified the onset of a strong El Niño event and outlined possible implications for rainfall, agriculture, water resources and energy. For August to October 2026, the agency forecast normal to above-normal rainfall across much of northern Nigeria, while parts of the South-West and Cross River State were expected to experience normal to below-normal rainfall. These projections highlight the possibility of different weather outcomes across the country. 1. Higher temperatures and health risks One major concern is the possibility of increased heat. In October 2026, the Climate Impact Lab projected that Nigeria could record an additional 31,400 heat-related deaths between September 2026 and February 2027, compared with an average year. The figure is a model-based estimate of potential excess deaths, not a confirmed death toll or a certainty that those deaths will occur. Extreme heat can cause dehydration, heat exhaustion and potentially fatal heatstroke, particularly among children, older people and outdoor workers. Health authorities should strengthen public awareness campaigns, issue timely heat warnings and prepare health facilities for heat-related emergencies. Residents should drink water regularly, seek shade, limit strenuous outdoor activities during the hottest hours where possible, and check on vulnerable relatives and neighbours. 2. Agriculture and food production Changes in rainfall can disrupt planting schedules and crop development. Prolonged dry spells or an early end to the rainy season could reduce yields, while excessive rainfall may cause flooding and damage farms. NiMet has identified possible agricultural risks in areas expecting below-normal rainfall, including parts of Borno and Yobe. Farmers should monitor updated forecasts, consider early-maturing or drought-tolerant crop varieties where appropriate, and seek advice from agricultural extension officers. In areas expecting heavier rainfall, maintaining drainage channels can help limit damage. Government agencies should also improve farmers’ access to timely weather information and agricultural advice. 3. Water supply and electricity generation Prolonged rainfall deficits can reduce river flows, reservoir levels and groundwater recharge, putting pressure on domestic water supplies and irrigation. Hydropower generation could also be affected if water inflows into dams decline. NiMet has identified reduced water availability and lower reservoir inflows as potential risks, although these do not confirm nationwide water shortages or electricity disruptions. Water authorities should monitor reservoirs and groundwater conditions, identify vulnerable communities and develop contingency plans. Residents can help by repairing leaking taps and avoiding unnecessary water waste. 4. Food prices and household expenses Adverse weather could reduce agricultural output, damage farms and disrupt transportation, placing pressure on food supplies and prices. However, El Niño alone does not mean food prices will rise nationwide. Harvests, storage, transport costs and wider market conditions will also influence prices. The government should monitor food supplies, support farmers in vulnerable areas and strengthen storage and distribution systems to reduce avoidable losses. How should Nigeria prepare? Preparation requires coordinated action by government agencies, state authorities, farmers, health workers, businesses and residents. NiMet should continue issuing updated, location-specific forecasts and ensure warnings reach rural communities and farmers, including those without reliable internet access. Health authorities should educate the public on heat-related illnesses and strengthen emergency responses, particularly for vulnerable populations. Agricultural ministries and extension officers should provide advice on planting dates, crop selection, irrigation and drainage based on current forecasts. Water agencies should monitor dams and reservoirs, reduce distribution losses and plan for communities that may face shortages. Authorities must also prepare for heavy rainfall and flooding rather than focus exclusively on drought. Government agencies, broadcasters and journalists should communicate climate information clearly, distinguish projections from confirmed events and update the public as conditions change. Does El Niño mean Nigeria is heading for disaster? Not necessarily. El Niño increases the likelihood of certain climate-related impacts but does not determine precisely what will happen in every state. The WMO has emphasised that even a very strong event does not produce equally severe effects everywhere. Local weather patterns and other climate drivers can alter its influence. Nigeria’s priority should be to identify areas most vulnerable to heat and rainfall changes and prepare accordingly. Following NiMet’s updates and taking practical precautions can help reduce risks to public health, agriculture, water resources and electricity generation. Ultimately, the challenge is not simply how strong El Niño becomes, but how effectively Nigeria prepares for its potential consequences. The post El Niño: What it means and how Nigerians should prepare appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Obsèques de Séné Diallo : émotion, témoignages poignants et appels à la solidarité lors du dernier hommage à l’animateur culturel
items.description: L’émotion était vive ce lundi 26 octobre 2026 à l’hôpital de l’amitié sino-guinéenne, à Conakry, lors de la levée du corps d’Aboubacar Diallo, plus connu sous le nom de Séné Diallo, journaliste et animateur culturel. Parents, personnalités publiques, journalistes, artistes, amis, collaborateurs et connaissances se sont mobilisés pour rendre un dernier hommage à celui qui a consacré une grande partie de sa vie à la promotion de la culture guinéenne. Entre témoignages poignants, souvenirs et appels à la solidarité envers sa famille, la cérémonie a été marquée par une profonde tristesse. Dans une atmosphère de recueillement, plusieurs intervenants se sont succédé pour retracer le parcours professionnel du défunt, saluer ses qualités humaines et évoquer les souvenirs laissés par celui dont la voix a accompagné des milliers d’auditeurs. Prenant la parole lors de ce symposium, Ibrahima Sory Traoré est revenu sur les grandes étapes de la vie de Séné Diallo, depuis son enfance à Fria jusqu’à son parcours dans les médias et la communication. Fils de Mamadi Diallo et de Binta Sané, Séné Diallo a grandi à Fria, où il s’était déjà distingué par son engagement envers les autres, notamment à travers l’enseignement bénévole du français et des mathématiques au collège Tito.Son parcours professionnel l’a ensuite conduit à Nostalgie Guinée, où il a exercé pendant près de dix ans, devenant une voix familière pour de nombreux auditeurs. En 2011, son talent a été récompensé par le Diassa d’or du meilleur animateur radio de Guinée.Également actif dans l’événementiel, il a travaillé dans plusieurs structures, notamment Celcom, Guicopress et Djoma Médias. «Il enseignait bénévolement le français et les mathématiques au collège Tito, sans rien attendre en retour. Il était déjà, avant le micro et les projecteurs, un homme qui donne. Sur Djoma Médias, il nous tendait chaque semaine le miroir de notre passé commun. Avec tendresse, il ravivait les airs, les visages et les instants que nous connaissions bien. Il était, en quelque sorte, le gardien de notre nostalgie collective », a souligné Traoré. Avec Sénémania, il ouvrait des scènes aux artistes guinéens. Combien d’entre eux lui doivent leurs premiers applaudissements ? Séné était dynamique, honnête, généreux, toujours soucieux de bien faire. Mais il était surtout un époux aimant et un père de trois enfants », a-t-il soutenu. S’adressant directement à la famille endeuillée, le PDG du site d’information Guinée7, Ibrahima Sory Traoré a rappelé que la disparition de Séné Diallo constituait une perte ressentie bien au-delà de son entourage immédiat:«À ses enfants, à sa sœur ici présente, à son frère aussi présent, à toute sa famille, votre peine est la nôtre. Toute une nation d’auditeurs pleure avec vous. Séné, tu as passé ta vie à donner la parole aux autres. Aujourd’hui, c’est nous qui parlons de toi et les mots nous manquent. Le studio est plutôt silencieux, mais ta voix restera dans chacun de nos souvenirs », a-t-il déclaré. Tous provenant de la cité des aluminium, M. Traoré a adressé son adieux : «Fria, qui t’a vu grandir, Fria, qui t’a tout donné et qui a tout reçu de toi, te dit merci. Repose en paix, guerrier. Qu’Allah t’accorde sa miséricorde. Va en paix, mon frère ! » De son côté, l’acteur culturel, écrivain et ancien ministre de la Jeunesse et des Sports, Fodeba Isto Keira, visiblement affecté par cette disparition, a rappelé les circonstances de sa rencontre avec Séné Diallo au début des années 2000, alors que ce dernier faisait ses premiers pas dans l’animation culturelle:« Notre jeune frère Séné, c’est difficile de témoigner, mais l’honnêteté intellectuelle m’oblige à dire que cet homme que nous voyons étalé ici m’a été présenté par Malick Kébé dans les années 2000, pour que, dans mes spectacles que j’organisais à l’époque, parce que j’étais très actif avant de prendre ma retraite de la scène, il puisse présenter les spectacles de musique urbaine », a-t-il expliqué. Évoquant cette génération de jeunes animateurs et journalistes culturels qui ont fait leurs premiers pas auprès des acteurs expérimentés du secteur, Fodéba Isto Keira a salué la mobilisation enregistrée autour du défunt, malgré le court délai entre l’annonce de son décès et l’organisation du symposium: «C’est l’occasion pour moi, ici, au moment où on se sépare, de présenter mes respectueuses condoléances à sa famille biologique, à l’ensemble de la presse nationale, parce que, malgré le temps court marquant l’annonce de son décès et la programmation de ce symposium, voyez déjà l’expression populaire à travers cette mobilisation de toutes les couches sociales de notre pays. Merci aux artistes, merci aux journalistes », a-t-il déclaré. Avant de terminer son intervention, il a invité les proches, les confrères et les acteurs culturels à accompagner la famille de Séné Diallo, particulièrement ses enfants.«Je finis par des prières pour que son âme repose en paix. Nous disons courage à son épouse, à toute sa famille, et chacun de nous pourra apporter ce qu’il peut à sa famille pour que les enfants puissent vivre décemment », a-t-il lancé. Un appel à la solidarité également porté par Patricia Adeline Lamah, ancienne ministre de la promotion féminine, coiffeuse, qui s’est exprimée en sa qualité de petite sœur et de protégée du défunt:«Je vais intervenir aujourd’hui en tant que petite sœur et protégée. C’est quelqu’un qui m’a toujours protégée, qui m’a toujours accompagnée. Quelle que soit la destination que je prends, il est toujours là avec moi. Je vais juste dire à tout le monde ici présent que, s’il avait une relation particulière avec chacun, c’était une lumière pour tout le monde. Mais avant tout, c’était un humain, quelqu’un qui aimait les gens. C’est quelqu’un qui aimait élever les gens », a-t-elle témoigné. Au-delà de cet hommage personnel, Patricia Adeline Lamah a surtout insisté sur la nécessité de ne pas abandonner les enfants laissés par le défunt.«Je voudrais vous dire de ne pas oublier ses enfants, parce qu’on savait que c’était un bon papa qui adorait ses enfants. Il part aujourd’hui, mais il a laissé ses représentants qui sont ses enfants. Nous ne les oublions surtout pas. Je prie vraiment que, là où tu pars, tu partages de l’amour, de la joie comme d’habitude, et que tu reposes en paix. Que Dieu ait ton âme. Là où tu es, tu seras l’animateur auprès du Seigneur », a-t-elle ajouté. Après ces témoignages et les derniers hommages rendus à l’hôpital de l’amitié sino-guinéenne, la dépouille d’Aboubacar Diallo l’auteur du slogan: «avant c’était mieux», a été conduite à Taouyah, dans le quartier de Rogbanè, où une dernière prière a été organisée avant son inhumation au cimetière du même nom. Le journaliste et animateur culturel y repose désormais, laissant derrière lui une veuve et trois enfants en bas âge, privés de leur époux et père. Une disparition douloureuse qui soulève également la question de l’avenir de cette famille, au cœur des appels à la solidarité lancés lors de la cérémonie. Si le micro de Fory Séné s’est définitivement tu, sa voix, son engagement en faveur de la culture guinéenne, les souvenirs et son énergie positive qu’il laisse à ses proches et collaborateurs continueront de résonner dans les mémoires. Mayi Cissé L’article Obsèques de Séné Diallo : émotion, témoignages poignants et appels à la solidarité lors du dernier hommage à l’animateur culturel est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: 2027: Rise Networks, INEC, Meta, Google, Microsoft join forces to launch #AI4Elections Hackathon
items.description: Rise Networks, in collaboration with the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Meta, Google, Microsoft and other partners, has launched the #AI4Elections Hackathon to develop artificial intelligence solutions aimed at strengthening Nigeria’s electoral process ahead of the 2027 general elections. The national, multidisciplinary and nonpartisan initiative will bring together technology developers, researchers, university students, electoral experts, civil society organisations and innovators to develop practical AI-powered tools addressing challenges associated with elections. Other partners include the International Centre for Investigative Reporting (ICIR), NITHUB at the University of Lagos, the Centre for Information Technology and Development (CITAD), CLEEN Foundation, Tap Initiative for Citizens’ Development, International Press Centre, Legal Naija, Ahmadu Bello University and the Federal University of Technology, Akure. The programme is supported by the MacArthur Foundation and Luminate and builds on Rise Networks’ experience developing Run-Am, an AI-powered misinformation detection and fact-checking mobile application used during the 2023 Nigerian elections. Applications opened on Thursday, October 22, 2026, and will close on November 12 at 11:59 p.m. West African Time. The programme will run from October 2026 to February 2027, with a national grand finale and innovation showcase scheduled for December 16 in Lagos. Speaking at a press conference in Abuja, the founder of Rise Networks, Dr Toyosi Akerele-Ogunsiji, said the initiative was designed to promote responsible AI innovation that protects electoral integrity and citizens’ rights. “Our ambition is not to introduce technology for technology’s sake. We are committed to promoting responsible AI innovation that respects the integrity of Nigeria’s electoral process, protects citizens’ rights, and prioritises transparency, privacy, and human oversight,” she said. “Innovation must strengthen our democracy, not create new vulnerabilities for it.” Akerele-Ogunsiji said Nigeria needed to harness emerging technologies to improve access to reliable information and strengthen public confidence in democratic institutions. “We must begin to harness the power of artificial intelligence to strengthen electoral integrity, expand access to information, and build greater public confidence in our democratic institutions,” she said. “The #AI4Elections Hackathon is an opportunity to bring our brightest minds together to develop solutions that respond to the realities of our electoral process.” The competition will focus on five principal areas: trustworthy electoral information; electoral data analysis, operational insights and decision support; inclusive and multilingual electoral and civic technology; electoral cybersecurity and resilience; and election observation and citizen accountability. Climate resilience and environmental innovation will also be considered as an optional cross-cutting area. Participants are expected to develop working solutions, including AI-enabled applications, software prototypes, data-analysis tools, multilingual interfaces and other technically credible products. Idea-only submissions, presentations and mock-ups without functional solutions will not be accepted. The hackathon is open to Nigerians aged 18 and above, including developers, AI engineers, data scientists, cybersecurity professionals, researchers, civic-tech innovators, electoral experts, product designers and public policy practitioners. Applications may be submitted by individuals or teams of up to four members, with team-matching support available for individual applicants. Entries must be submitted in English, and projects that have already received grants, awards or recognition in previous competitions are ineligible. Speaking at the event, Dr Lawrence Bayode said the growing influence of AI on elections made it necessary for Nigeria to develop solutions that preserve electoral credibility. “The question before us is no longer whether AI has a role to play in an election, but how we can harness its potential without compromising the integrity, transparency and credibility of the electoral process,” he said. Meta’s Head of Public Policy for Anglophone West Africa, Sade Dada, said the company would work with INEC to promote reliable election information and tackle false claims, including fake images and videos generated with AI. She highlighted Meta’s “Remove, Reduce and Inform” approach and GovGuide Nigeria, an AI-powered chatbot that provides government information in English, Hausa, Igbo and Yoruba. Dada stressed that AI tools used during elections must remain politically neutral and operate under human oversight, adding that Nigeria’s experience could offer lessons for other countries. “The 2027 elections matter far beyond Nigeria’s borders. If Nigeria gets it right on trustworthy information, the continent will learn from it and, indeed, the world,” she said. Other speakers, including Lagos Business School Dean, Prof. Olayinka David-West, and legal practitioner Tsema Ede, said AI could improve election results management but emphasised the need for transparency and public trust. The hackathon has a total cash prize pool of ₦10 million. The overall winner will receive ₦4 million, while the second- and third-place winners will receive ₦2.5 million and ₦1.5 million, respectively. Four additional special innovation awards, each worth ₦500,000, will recognise outstanding work in research and policy innovation, electoral and civic inclusion, responsible AI and safety, and cybersecurity and resilience. Entries will be assessed based on technical functionality and innovation, relevance to electoral challenges, practical usefulness, cybersecurity, privacy, responsible AI, scalability, feasibility, demonstration and documentation. Rise Networks said the programme would also include an AI4Elections Development Hub to support the testing and refinement of promising solutions, alongside a Community of Practice to sustain collaboration among innovators, researchers, mentors and electoral stakeholders beyond the competition. The organisers stressed that the initiative would not support partisan campaign technology, voter manipulation or interference with electoral administration. Participants are also prohibited from conducting unauthorised tests of live electoral systems or accessing institutional infrastructure. Winning the competition will not automatically authorise the deployment of any solution in an election, as future institutional pilots will remain subject to relevant legal, technical, institutional and security approvals. Interested applicants can obtain further information and apply through ai4elections.risenetworks.org. items.title: 2027: ADC dismisses APC’s 2m votes target for Tinubu in Jigawa‎
items.description: By Muhammad Inuwa ‎The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has expressed confidence that its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, will win Jigawa State in the 2027 general elections, dismissing the All Progressives Congress (APC)’s target of delivering two million votes for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu as unrealistic. ‎The ADC candidate for Ringim/Taura Federal Constituency in Jigawa State, Hon. Shehu Sule Udi, stated this while reacting to the Jigawa APC’s declaration that it would deliver two million votes for Tinubu’s re-election. ‎Udi argued that the number of registered voters in Jigawa State made the APC’s target questionable, describing the declaration as political propaganda. ‎According to him, figures displayed by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) showed that Jigawa had 2,807,811 registered voters. ‎“This clearly shows that the party is just making propaganda,” he said. ‎“Look at how our presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, and other candidates in ADC are gaining support across Jigawa State every day. For somebody to tell you that they will deliver two million votes to Tinubu is ridiculous,” Udi stated. ‎He claimed that residents of the state were dissatisfied with the current administration because of the economic hardship facing Nigerians. ‎“People of Jigawa State are tired of this administration. They have suffered enough, and no reasonable person will vote for the APC in the coming election. ‎“Our presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, will win Jigawa State with massive votes and defeat President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said. ‎Udi maintained that the ADC remained a credible alternative capable of addressing the economic challenges facing the country. ‎He expressed confidence that the growing support for the party across Jigawa State would translate into electoral victory in 2027. ‎The ADC candidate spoke while welcoming defectors from other political parties in Ringim and Taura Local Government Areas, describing their decision to join the party as a boost to its political strength ahead of the elections. items.title: Govt orders review of existing drug pricing formula to ensure medicines are priced fairly
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The government on Monday warned that drug prices must not be increased without valid justification and ordered a review of the existing pricing formula to ensure medicines are priced fairly without creating unnecessary hurdles for patients, importers or the pharmaceutical industry. Economic Affairs Minister Ahad Cheema, who chaired a meeting of the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan (Drap), directed officials to expedite the processing of pending drug-pricing cases after being briefed that their case-by-case evaluation was almost complete. The minister appreciated the progress and acknowledged the efforts of Climate Change Minister Dr Musadik Malik and Drap officials in completing the evaluation. Health Secretary Momin Agha, Drap Chief Executive Officer Dr Obaidullah Malik and other senior officials also attended the meeting. The meeting was also informed that sufficient quantities of the trivalent influenza vaccine recommended by the World Health Organisation (WHO) were available in the market. Drap had withdrawn the hardship case relating to the vaccine as its prices were controlled in the international market. Officials told the meeting that Drap was reviewing the existing drug-pricing formula and examining provisions that could hinder the determination of fair and accurate prices. Cheema suggested that Drap consider subscribing to specialised international databases on drug prices to strengthen independent assessment and provide more reliable benchmarks for pricing decisions. “Public facilitation should remain the government’s top priority,” he emphasised, adding that any increase in medicine prices without valid justification was unacceptable. The minister said price comparisons with other countries could provide useful benchmarks, but stressed the need for independent checks and balances in the pricing process. Cheema ordered that the pricing mechanism should remain people-centred while avoiding unnecessary barriers for importers and pharmaceutical companies. Pharma industry’s perspective Meanwhile, the Pakistan Pharmaceutical Manufacturers Association (PPMA) urged the government to engage industry in the formula review so that the outcome could be workable and sustainable. PPMA Vice Chairman Usman Shaukat told Dawn that the pharmaceutical industry fully shared the government’s objective that medicines must remain affordable and accessible to every Pakistani. “No responsible manufacturer seeks an unjustified price increase, and we welcome Senator Ahad Cheema’s direction to expedite pending pricing cases and to review the pricing formula. A fair, transparent and predictable mechanism serves patients and industry alike,” he said. “However, affordability and availability go hand in hand. The real threat to patients is not a justified price adjustment but a medicine disappearing from the shelf.” Shaukat noted that products become unviable when the cost of active ingredients, packaging, energy, freight and compliance rises — most of which is imported and relies on the dollar — and prices remain frozen for years. “Manufacturers are then forced to stop production, which creates shortages and pushes patients towards costlier imported alternatives, smuggled stock or spurious medicines,“ he explained. Shaukat said that the industry supports the use of international benchmarks and independent databases, provided comparisons account for the cost of doing business within Pakistan, high financing costs, exchange-rate exposure and the fact that Pakistani medicine prices are already among the lowest in the region. “Benchmarks should be a tool for fairness, not a ceiling that ignores input costs,” he highlighted. “PPMA proposes that the revised formula include a clear, time-bound and rules-based mechanism, including periodic CPI and cost-linked adjustments, so that hardship cases do not pile up and decisions are not delayed for years,” Shaukat added.

items.title: 2027: INEC seeks inclusive polls, sensitises PWDs, Electoral Officers in Benue
items.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Benue State has held a sensitisation workshop for Persons With Disabilities (PWDs), Electoral Officers (EOs) and Disability Desk Officers, targeting improved accessibility, effective deployment of assistive devices and inclusive participation in the 2027 general elections. The workshop, organised by the commission ahead of the elections, was designed to strengthen stakeholders’ understanding of disability inclusion, electoral rights and interventions aimed at ensuring that eligible voters with disabilities can participate fully in the electoral process. Speaking at the event, the Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Benue State, Mallam Aminu Idris, said INEC was committed to engaging stakeholders to ensure the conduct of free, fair and credible elections, stressing that inclusivity was equally essential to achieving that objective. The REC said, “it is not just to have free, fair and credible elections. It is to have inclusive elections. If you leave a chunk of your population out, you cannot be talking about free, fair and credible elections.” He added that INEC had a dedicated department responsible for inclusivity and addressing the concerns of disadvantaged groups to ensure everyone had the opportunity to participate in the electoral process. He explained that the commission identifies voters with disabilities during registration to enable it determine the needs of different polling units and deploy appropriate materials and assistance noting that “the objective is to ensure that eligible voters who have registered and obtained their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) did not encounter unnecessary difficulties while voting.” On the participation of Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), the REC disclosed that INEC had conducted registration exercises at IDP locations in collaboration with non-governmental organisations interested in encouraging voter registration. He said “our officials visited the locations on two consecutive days to register eligible voters to ensure that they exercise their franchise during the election.” Addressing concerns over the collection of PVCs, Idris said “cards belonging to those who registered during the first phase of the Continuous Voter Registration exercise, conducted between August and December 2025, are available for collection at the local government level.” He added that cards for those who registered in 2026 would be ready subsequently before the elections. In his goodwill message, the Benue State Director of the National Orientation Agency (NOA), Comrade Mark Dewua, commended INEC for the initiative, saying “inclusive electoral participation is essential to strengthening democracy.” He urged for “accessible polling units, effective communication of electoral information, appropriate deployment of assistive devices and respectful treatment of voters with disabilities.” Dewua, who reaffirmed NOA’s commitment to collaborating with INEC on voter education and public enlightenment, urged political parties, civil society organisations, security agencies and the media to “work together to remove barriers to electoral participation.” He also encouraged PWDs to obtain their PVCs, verify their registration details and participate peacefully in the forthcoming elections. Similarly, the Chairman of the Joint National Association of Persons With Disabilities (JONAPWD), Benue State, Onah Adeyi, described the workshop as groundbreaking, noting that it provided an opportunity for PWDs to engage directly with INEC officials on issues affecting their participation in elections. Adeyi, who disclosed that “PWDs in the state have over 3,000 PVCs, and I am optimistic that the figure would increase following the ongoing collection exercise.” He urged INEC to consider qualified persons with disabilities for appointment as electoral officers, provide appropriate assistive devices for different disability groups and ensure that PWDs exercised their constitutional rights to vote and participate in the electoral process. Speaking on the objectives of the workshop, INEC Benue State Disability Desk Officer, Mnena Akuma, said “it is designed to strengthen stakeholders’ understanding of disability inclusion, accessibility and the effective deployment of the commission’s interventions throughout the electoral cycle.” She cited Section 54 of the Electoral Act, 2026, the Discrimination Against Persons With Disabilities (Prohibition) Act, 2018, and INEC’s framework on access and participation of PWDs as key instruments underpinning the initiative. Akuma listed the objectives of the workshop to include improving understanding of barriers confronting PWDs, strengthening the capacity of electoral officers to deploy assistive materials, promoting inclusive voter education and mobilising voters across disability groups. She identified the Braille Ballot Guide for visually impaired voters, EC30 written instruction posters for deaf voters, magnifying glasses for persons with visual impairment and albinism, and voter education materials in accessible formats as some of the interventions. She added that the workshop would strengthen collaboration between INEC, JONAPWD, Organisations of Persons with Disabilities and cluster heads, while generating practical recommendations to improve accessibility, compliance and inclusive participation ahead of the 2027 general elections. The post 2027: INEC seeks inclusive polls, sensitises PWDs, Electoral Officers in Benue appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 2027: INEC puts preliminary voters’ register online, publishes final document Dec. 15
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has made the Preliminary Register of Voters for the 2027 General Election available on its online platform, following concerns raised by some stakeholders and in preparation for the certification and publication of the Final Register of Voters on December 15. The register can now be accessed at https://display.inecnigeria.org. It is the same list that was earlier displayed at Registration Areas nationwide. National Commissioner and Chairman, Information and Voter Education Committee at INEC, Mohammed Kudu Haruna, said in a statement on Monday that the Commission “has taken note of the concerns expressed by Nigerians and other stakeholders regarding the desirability of making the Register accessible through its online platform in addition to the physical display already conducted.” “Accordingly, and in furtherance of its commitment to transparency, accessibility and public confidence in the electoral process, the Commission has decided to make available on its online platform https://display.inecnigeria.org the same Preliminary Register of Voters earlier displayed at the Registration Areas,” he said. Haruna recalled that the physical display was held in accordance with Section 19 of the Electoral Act, 2026, from 9th to 15th October, 2026. According to him, the exercise provided “registered voters the opportunity to inspect their particulars and submit claims and objections as prescribed by law.” He said the online publication does not replace the exercise already carried out. “This additional measure complements the physical display already undertaken and is intended to facilitate wider public access to the Register,” he said. The Commission said it is still processing the claims and objections that arose from the display. “Meanwhile, the Commission continues to process claims and objections arising from the exercise in accordance with the Electoral Act, 2026, preparatory to the certification and publication of the Final Register of Voters on 15th December 2026. “The Commission appreciates the continued interest and constructive engagement of Nigerians and stakeholders and reiterates its commitment to transparency, accountability and the faithful implementation of the Electoral Act, 2026 in delivering credible elections,” he said. items.title: L’Algérie inaugure la deuxième plus grande centrale solaire en Afrique
items.description: La centrale solaire photovoltaïque d’El Foulia dans la wilaya d’El Oued a été inaugurée, aujourd’hui lundi, par le ministre de l’Énergie et des Énergies renouvelables Mourad Adjal. D’une capacité de 300 mégawatts, cette centrale, située dans la commune de Guemar, est la plus grande en Algérie et la 2ᵉ en Afrique, a déclaré M. Adjal. « La centrale d’El Foulia a été réalisée avec un partenaire chinois , mais le gros du travail a été fait par les bras des Algériens. La gestion de la centrale est confiée aux compétences nationales », a déclaré le ministre de l’Énergie, en marge de la cérémonie d’inauguration officielle. Deux nouvelles centrales solaires mises en service à El Oued durant le premier trimestre 2027 Il a rappelé que la mise en service de la station est intervenue, pendant l’été dernier, pour faire face aux pics de consommation d’électricité. Deux autres centrales de 200 MW et 100 MW seront mises en service dans la wilaya d’El Oued, durant le premier trimestre de l’année 2027, a-t-il annoncé. La centrale d’El Foulia vient renforcer le parc photovoltaïque algérien qui a vu, au cours de l’année 2026, la mise en service de deux nouvelles centrales à Tendla (El-Meghaier) et à El-Ghrous (Biskra) et qui disposent, chacune, d’une capacité de 200 mégawatts. Le programme national de développement des énergies renouvelables prévoit la production de 15.000 MW d’énergie solaire à l'horizon 2035. La première phase prévoit la réalisation de 21 centrales solaires photovoltaïques dans 14 wilayas, d'une capacité totale de 3.200 MW, dont 760 MWc sont déjà entrés en service. L’article L’Algérie inaugure la deuxième plus grande centrale solaire en Afrique est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Prof. Ochefu rejects appointment to NDC National Campaign Council
items.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi Professor of Economic History and Strategic Studies at Rev. Fr. Moses Orshio Adasu University, Makurdi, Prof. Yakubu Ochefu, has rejected his purported appointment to the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) National Campaign Council, insisting that he is not a member of the party. Ochefu said he was neither consulted before his name was included in the list of members of the campaign council circulating on social media nor did he give his consent to the appointment. The university don, who is also the National Chairman of the Association of Nigerian Universities Alumni (ANUA) and President-General of Ochetoha K’Idoma, said his leadership positions required him to remain non-partisan, as the memberships of both organisations cut across political parties. In a statement he personally signed, Prof. Ochefu said, “My attention has been drawn to a list circulating on social media, titled ‘Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) National Campaign Council’, which names me as a member of its National Campaign Caucus. “I wish to inform the public that I am not a member of the NDC and have never been. “I was not consulted before my name was included, nor did I give consent. “I have written to the Chairman of the Council to decline the appointment and to request that my name be withdrawn and a revised list published. “As National Chairman of the Association of Nigerian Universities Alumni, ANUA, and President-General of Ochetoha K’Idoma, I lead organisations whose members cut across all political parties. These offices require me to remain non-partisan, and I intend to honour that obligation. “I thank all who reached out for clarification, and ask that you disregard the list insofar as it concerns me.” The post Prof. Ochefu rejects appointment to NDC National Campaign Council appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ADC to APC: Nigerians suffer, your youth leaders ride N1bn SUVs
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike The African Democratic Congress, ADC, has slammed the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, over the reported distribution of seven luxury sports utility vehicles (SUVs) worth about N1 billion to its youth leaders, accusing the ruling party of prioritising political mobilisation over the hardship facing Nigerians. The opposition party said the reported distribution exposed the contradiction between the economic sacrifices Nigerians are being asked to make and the privileges enjoyed by the ruling party’s political operatives, with millions struggling to afford food, transportation and other necessities. In a statement on Monday, ADC National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, said the development raised questions about the APC’s priorities as it prepares for the 2027 general elections. “President Tinubu asks Nigerians to endure hardship while his party distributes luxury vehicles to its political operatives. Apparently, sacrifice is for ordinary Nigerians, while luxury is reserved for those working to keep the APC in power,” he said. Abdullahi said the ruling party had mobilised resources for its political machinery without offering a convincing answer to the rising cost of living. “The APC has found the resources to move its campaign officials around Nigeria. What it has failed to find is a convincing way to make life affordable for the Nigerians whose votes it now seeks,” he said. The ADC also questioned the rationale for providing the vehicles for grassroots mobilisation ahead of the 2027 elections when youth unemployment and economic hardship remain major concerns. “Seven APC youth leaders can receive luxury vehicles, but millions of young Nigerians are still waiting for the jobs, opportunities and economic relief they were promised. Is this the APC’s idea of youth empowerment?” Abdullahi asked. The party demanded disclosure of the source of funding for the vehicles, including whether public resources were involved. “Nigerians deserve to know who paid for these vehicles. Until that question is answered, the ruling party cannot dismiss legitimate concerns about its priorities,” Abdullahi said. The post ADC to APC: Nigerians suffer, your youth leaders ride N1bn SUVs appeared first on Vanguard News .
