items.title: ADC fires back at APC over unpaid salary claims
items.description: dares ruling party to defend record By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has challenged the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to defend its record in government rather than make allegations against opposition parties, dismissing claims of unpaid salaries within the ADC as false and politically motivated. The party said the allegation was an attempt to divert attention from the economic hardship, rising cost of living, unemployment and insecurity confronting Nigerians, warning that the 2027 election debate should centre on the Tinubu administration’s performance. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC challenged the APC Presidential Campaign Council to produce evidence to substantiate its allegation, describing the claim as an attempt to distract Nigerians from the government’s record. “If the APC has any credible evidence to support its claims, it should produce it rather than continue to insult Nigerians with fabricated stories masquerading as press statements,” Abdullahi said. On the issues it believes should dominate public debate, the ADC said: “The real issue is the cost of living. The real issue is the absence of jobs and opportunities for our young people. The real issue is the insecurity that continues to threaten lives, livelihoods, and communities across the country.” The party also accused the APC of preparing for the 2027 elections by attacking opposition parties rather than presenting its achievements. “It is becoming increasingly clear that the APC has decided to run its 2027 campaign on allegations against the opposition rather than achievements of its own. That is what happens when a government has spent years making promises it cannot keep and excuses it cannot defend,” Abdullahi said. The ADC spokesman urged Minister of Information, Alake, and other APC officials to explain why Nigerians should support another term for the ruling party after three years of economic hardship and insecurity. “The APC may control the machinery of government, but it cannot control the lived experiences of Nigerians,” he said. Abdullahi said the ADC would remain focused on holding the Tinubu administration accountable, insisting that allegations against the opposition would not displace the economic concerns shaping public debate. “If the APC has a record to defend, let it defend it. If it has solutions, let it present them. But it should stop insulting the intelligence of Nigerians with these increasingly desperate distractions,” he added. The party maintained that the cost of living would remain central to its campaign, positioning the economic consequences of the Tinubu administration’s policies as a defining issue in the 2027 election. I urge the DSS and all sister security apparatuses to launch an immediate, aggressive manhunt for the criminals. “To the good people of Enugu State, I urge them to remain calm, vigilant, and resilient and not be intimidated by the desperate rants of cowards while also reporting any suspicious movements or individuals to the nearest security agency immediately. Let me make it clear that Enugu State belongs to the peaceful and law-abiding individuals and forces of terror will always be defeated,” Onoh said. items.title: Can point-of-care testing improve early detection of chronic kidney disease in Africa?
items.description: Introduction Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a growing public health concern in Africa, where early detection remains challenging due to persistent gaps in access to diagnostic services and routine screening. A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis estimated that CKD (stages 1-5) affects approximately 13.7% of adults across 19 African countries 1 . Limited access to diagnostic services, the cost of laboratory investigations, and gaps in routine screening can delay the identification of kidney abnormalities, particularly among high-risk populations, including people living with hypertension, diabetes, and cardiovascular diseases 1–3 . Evidence also indicates that risk-factor-based screening in primary care can support the early detection of CKD, reinforcing the importance of improving access to kidney health assessment in underserved settings 4 . This raises an important question: Could point-of-care testing (POCT) help bridge the gap between kidney disease risk and timely diagnosis in Africa? What role could point-of-care testing play? Point-of-care testing refers to any diagnostic test performed near the patient, rather than exclusively in centralised laboratories 5,6 . It is commonly referred to as “bedside testing” 7 . By providing results closer to the point of care, POCT may reduce delays associated with specimen transportation and result reporting and support more timely clinical decisions. For kidney health, two important areas of assessment are: Blood creatinine: Used to estimate kidney filtration function through a calculated estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). Urine albumin: Helps identify kidney damage. Measuring the urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR) is particularly useful for assessing albuminuria. Evidence suggests that POCT can support CKD screening by enabling creatinine and urine albumin measurements in community and primary healthcare settings, particularly where access to conventional laboratory services is limited 8–10 . Although selected POCT devices have demonstrated promising diagnostic performance, accuracy varies across technologies, with some exhibiting measurement bias and reduced sensitivity. The 2024 Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) guideline highlights the potential role of point-of-care testing (POCT) in CKD screening, particularly for measuring creatinine, urine albumin or urine protein in settings with limited access to laboratory services or where decentralised testing can facilitate earlier detection, reduce delays in obtaining test results, and support timely clinical decision-making and referral 9 . The World Health Organization has also included point-of-care creatinine testing in its Model List of Essential In Vitro Diagnostics for use in settings such as community outreach and primary healthcare facilities without laboratories 11 . These recommendations provide a strong rationale for exploring decentralised kidney health testing in Africa. However, the value of POCT extends beyond the availability of a rapid test; it depends on whether the test can be integrated into a functioning pathway for screening, confirmation, referral, and treatment. Five considerations for implementing kidney health POCT in Africa 1. Diagnostic performance and clinical utility Not all POCT devices perform equally, and the convenience of rapid testing should not be confused with diagnostic accuracy. Devices must be evaluated against appropriate laboratory algorithms and standard guidelines, such as the World Health Organization’s (WHO) REASSURED criteria (Real-time connectivity, Ease of specimen collection, Affordability, Sensitivity, Specificity, User-friendliness, Rapidity and robustness, Equipment-free, and Deliverable to end-users), with attention to analytical performance, clinical sensitivity and specificity, and the potential consequences of false-positive and false-negative results 12–14 . For example, if a point-of-care creatinine diagnostic underestimates a patient’s serum creatinine concentration, the calculated estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) may be falsely reassuring, potentially resulting in missed kidney dysfunction and delayed referral. Conversely, overestimation of creatinine may produce an artificially low eGFR, leading to unnecessary referrals, additional investigations, unnecessary costs, and patient anxiety. Similarly, a urine albumin screening device that produces a false-negative result may fail to identify albuminuria in a patient with diabetes or hypertension, whereas a false-positive result may lead to unnecessary follow-up investigations. These highlight that the clinical value of POCTs depends not only on the speed of testing but also on the accuracy of results and the extent to which measurement errors may influence clinical decisions. For creatinine screening, the results are recommended to be used to estimate the glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) using an appropriate equation, with abnormal findings prompting further clinical assessment and confirmatory testing where indicated 9 . For urine albumin screening, quantitative measurement and calculation of the urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR) provide more clinically useful information than a simple positive or negative result 9 . However, a positive result from an initial qualitative screening test should prompt quantitative assessment to determine the extent of albuminuria. Where initial screening suggests albuminuria or reduced kidney function, confirmatory testing using appropriate laboratory methods and repeat assessment, where indicated, are essential before establishing a diagnosis of chronic kidney disease (CKD). Quality assurance, staff training, device maintenance, and external quality assessment are also crucial to ensuring the reliability of POCT results and supporting appropriate clinical decision-making 15,16 . 2. Affordability and equitable access The potential of POCT lies partly in its ability to bring diagnostic services closer to people who face geographical, financial, or health-system barriers to laboratory testing. In rural and hard-to-reach communities, and resource-constrained primary healthcare facilities, decentralised testing could reduce the need for some patients to travel to higher-level facilities solely to obtain initial kidney function measurements. However, an abnormal POCT result requires further laboratory investigations to confirm kidney abnormalities, assess their severity, and guide clinical management 9 . If patients cannot afford these additional tests, the benefits of initial screening may be limited, potentially leaving suspected cases undiagnosed or delaying appropriate care. The cost-effectiveness of implementing POCT for kidney disease should therefore be evaluated by considering the costs of equipment, consumables, staff training, quality assurance, maintenance, confirmatory testing, and follow-up care 17 . Affordability should be assessed across the entire diagnostic pathway, not simply in terms of the purchase price of a POCT device. This includes determining whether patients can afford confirmatory investigations and subsequent care, and whether health systems can sustainably finance these services. Integrating POCT into existing primary healthcare services, alongside appropriate financing and referral arrangements, may help minimise out-of-pocket expenditure and ensure that abnormal screening results lead to timely diagnosis and care 3. Integration of POCT into primary healthcare through task sharing, follow-up and referral pathways A positive screening result is only the beginning of the diagnostic process. Patients need access to clinical assessment, confirmatory investigations, appropriate referral, and treatment. This is particularly important because CKD is defined by abnormalities of kidney structure or function that persist for at least three months 1 . A single abnormal creatinine, eGFR, or urine albumin result does not automatically establish chronic kidney disease; the finding may reflect an acute or temporary abnormality 9 . Consequently, implementation strategies should clearly define who will be screened, how abnormal results will be communicated, when testing should be repeated, and how patients will be linked to appropriate care. Without these arrangements, decentralised testing may identify abnormalities without ensuring that patients receive the care they need. Many hard-to-reach communities across Africa face limited access to conventional laboratory services because of geographical barriers, inadequate diagnostic infrastructure, workforce shortages, and travel costs 18,19 . POCT could improve access to kidney health assessment within primary healthcare and chronic disease management services, particularly for people living with hypertension and diabetes. Task shifting and empowering community health workers (CHWs) could further extend these services by equipping appropriately trained personnel to support risk assessment, conduct approved screening tests where permitted, provide health education, and facilitate referral and follow-up. Such an approach could bring kidney health screening closer to underserved populations while reducing pressure on overstretched health professionals. However, implementation requires structured training, clear scopes of practice, supervision, quality assurance, and reliable referral pathways 9 . Patients with abnormal screening results should receive counselling, clinical assessment, and appropriate confirmatory testing, with urgent referral for markedly reduced eGFR, significant albuminuria, or other concerning findings. In settings where laboratories are distant, CHWs could help coordinate specimen transportation, remind patients about follow-up appointments, track referrals, and communicate results in collaboration with primary healthcare teams. They should not independently diagnose CKD or make clinical decisions beyond their training and authorised scope of practice. Importantly, a single abnormal POCT result does not establish CKD, which generally requires evidence of kidney abnormalities persisting for at least three months 1,9 . Integrating task-shared POCT into primary healthcare, supported by affordable confirmatory testing and clear referral protocols, could help translate improved screening access into timely diagnosis and appropriate care. 4. Multimorbidity and integrated screening Kidney health should not be considered in isolation from other chronic conditions. People living with diabetes, hypertension, HIV, and other long-term conditions may require assessment for kidney disease as part of their ongoing care. Integrating kidney health assessment into existing primary healthcare services could create opportunities to identify multiple conditions through coordinated screening and follow-up. Such an approach may reduce fragmented care and make better use of existing healthcare resources. However, integrated screening models must be evaluated to establish whether they improve detection, acceptability, linkage to care, and health outcomes without placing excessive demands on patients and healthcare workers 20 . 5. Home-based testing, self-testing and decentralised monitoring Home-based kidney health testing and monitoring may involve two distinct approaches: patient-performed self-testing, in which individuals conduct tests and interpret results at home, and healthcare worker-led testing during home visits, in which trained personnel perform tests and support result interpretation, counselling, and referral. Both approaches could extend kidney health assessment beyond conventional healthcare facilities, particularly for people at increased risk of chronic kidney disease (CKD), including those living with diabetes, hypertension, or other chronic conditions 8 . However, their suitability depends on the intended users, the type of test, and the clinical purpose. Technologies intended for self-testing require validation for use by non-professionals, with clear instructions on sample collection, test performance, result interpretation, and when to seek professional care 21 . Healthcare worker-led testing, meanwhile, requires appropriate training, supervision, and quality assurance to ensure reliable testing and referral 21 . The clinical value of both approaches also depends on affordability, user literacy, quality assurance, data privacy, and access to confirmatory testing and follow-up care 21 . These considerations are particularly important in resource-constrained settings, where identifying a potential kidney abnormality may not lead to timely clinical assessment or treatment. Healthcare worker-led home visits may help address some barriers to self-testing by providing assistance with test procedures, explaining results, and facilitating referrals; however, this approach depends on workforce availability and sustainable implementation. Furthermore, because CKD requires evidence of kidney abnormalities persisting for at least three months, a single abnormal home-test result cannot independently establish a diagnosis 9 . Home-based kidney testing, either patient-led or trained personnel-led should therefore be evaluated as a potential complement to established diagnostic and clinical pathways, rather than a replacement for professional assessment, confirmatory testing, and ongoing care. Moving from promising technologies to effective implementation From a health systems and implementation science perspective, the key question is whether POCT for CKD can be implemented reliably, affordably, equitably, and sustainably in African healthcare settings. Future research should assess the diagnostic accuracy and clinical utility of kidney function and urine albumin tests in African populations, their cost-effectiveness compared with conventional laboratory-based pathways, and their acceptability among patients and healthcare workers. It should also examine the feasibility of integrating CKD screening into primary healthcare and multimorbidity programs, including home-based monitoring where appropriate, and evaluate whether referral, confirmatory testing, and follow-up systems ensure that people with abnormal results receive timely care. Addressing procurement, supply chains, staff competencies, quality assurance, and health financing will be essential to support sustainable implementation and equitable scale-up of CKD POCT, particularly in underserved communities in Africa. Conclusion POCT has the potential to support earlier identification of kidney abnormalities in Africa by bringing selected diagnostic services closer to patients and primary healthcare facilities, particularly in underserved communities where access to conventional laboratory services is limited. However, its contribution to CKD screening will depend on diagnostic accuracy, affordability, quality assurance, confirmatory testing, effective referral pathways, and integration into routine healthcare. Moving beyond the availability of testing technologies towards reliable diagnostic pathways is essential to ensure that people with abnormal screening results receive appropriate clinical assessment, follow-up, and timely care. Greater research, implementation, and policy attention is therefore needed to establish how kidney health POCT can be integrated sustainably into primary healthcare and multimorbidity screening programs across African settings. Dr Evans Duah is the Head of Technology and Innovation at Kidney Research initiative Ghana. He is a Medical Laboratory Scientist and Public Health researcher. He specialises in point-of-care diagnostics, implementation science, and health systems research. His work focuses on improving access to accurate, affordable, and equitable diagnostic services, particularly in primary healthcare and resource-constrained settings across Africa. https://www.linkedin.com/in/evans-duah-75107649

items.title: 5 prominent Obidient members missing from NDC presidential campaign council
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has unveiled its 2027 presidential campaign council, naming flagbearer, Peter Obi and National Leader Seriake Dickson among its leaders. However, several prominent members of the Obidient movement who have actively and publicly supported Obi in the past are absent from the published list. The absence of such individuals is notable because they have either supported the NDC presidential candidate or taken part in the political movement in different ways, with their public profiles ranging from campaign activism and digital mobilisation to formal movement leadership. The list the party published on Sunday names the campaign caucus, advisory council, directorates and state coordinators. It also includes Obi and other senior party figures, but omits a few influential figures who have actively backed the Obidient movement in recent years. Here are five prominent Obidient movement members omitted from the NDC 2027 presidential campaign council. 1 . Moses Paul (Dr. Mo) Moses Paul, popularly known as Dr. Mo, has held formal leadership roles in the Obidient movement. He was identified as its Secretary General in 2025 and appointed National Coordinator in October 2026, while his predecessor, Yunusa Tanko, took on a role as an adviser to Obi. Dr. Mo rose to national prominence as the convener of the Free Nigeria Movement and a key organizer of youth-led mobilization and rallies supporting Peter Obi’s 2023 presidential campaign under the Labour Party. Obi also publicly backed Paul’s bid for chairman of the Abuja Municipal Area Council, saying he would campaign for him. Paul’s omission from the released council list stands out given his current leadership role in the movement and his previous candidacy with Obi’s support. 2. Aisha Yesufu Campaign activist and NDC member Aisha Yesufu served on Obi’s 2023 Labor Party presidential campaign team and was one of the prominent public voices backing his candidacy. She has also described the Obidient movement as part of a broader wave of political engagement after the #EndSARS protests, rather than a movement created by Obi. In May 2026, Yesufu joined the NDC, saying her political choices had been guided by her support for Obi. She declared for the FCT Senate seat but later withdrew from the race after internal party decisions on primaries. Her absence from the campaign council is notable given her past campaign role, movement profile and NDC membership. 3. Precious Oruche (Mama Pee) Precious Oruche, popularly known as Mama Pee, is regularly identified in news reports as an Obidient activist, grassroots organizer, social influencer, and an outspoken supporter of Obi. In 2025, the movement publicly supported her after a reported incident involving factional Labour Party chairman Julius Abure. Oruche has continued to use her public platform to advocate for Obi and remains a visible voice in Obi’s support base. However, her name does not appear on the NDC’s released campaign council list. 4. Peter Akah (Randy Peterz) Peter Akah, also known as Randy Peterz, is a political activist, digital content creator, and one of the most vocal defenders of Peter Obi and the Obidient movement. Akah’s public political work has included online mobilisation and civic engagement. Media reports described him and Oruche (Mama Pee)as prominent Obidient members and Obi supporters. His public association with Obi and the movement is documented, including being associated with Obidient Connect, a group supporting Obi’s 2027 campaign. The group has promoted voter participation, including urging Nigerians in the diaspora to help people at home get to the polls. 5. Isaac Fayose Fayose, the younger brother of former Ekiti State Governor Ayodele Fayose, has publicly said he campaigned for Obi in 2023, spent his own money in support of the campaign and made his hotel available for Obidient meetings in Ibadan. Isaac Fayose He has also said he took part in a protest in support of the movement. In July 2026, Obi visited Fayose after Fayose spoke publicly about his campaign efforts. Fayose subsequently reaffirmed his support for Obi. As with the other names, the released council list does not include him. The post 5 prominent Obidient members missing from NDC presidential campaign council appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ballon d’Or 2026 : Achraf Hakimi termine à la 13e place
items.description: Achraf Hakimi, latéral du Paris Saint-Germain, se classe à la 13e place du Ballon d’Or 2026, selon le classement communiqué par Hesport. Le défenseur poursuit ainsi sa présence parmi les joueurs reconnus sur la scène internationale. Achraf Hakimi figure à la 13e place du classement du Ballon d’Or 2026. Le latéral marocain du Paris Saint-Germain confirme ainsi son statut parmi les joueurs majeurs de sa génération, grâce à ses performances avec le club parisien et la sélection nationale. Cette distinction intervient alors que l’international marocain continue de se démarquer par sa polyvalence, sa capacité à contribuer aux phases offensives et son engagement dans les tâches défensives. Au cours de la saison 2026-2027, Hakimi a disputé 11 rencontres avec le PSG toutes compétitions confondues, dont neuf en tant que titulaire, pour un total de 833 minutes de jeu, selon les données arrêtées à la fin du mois d’octobre. Le Marocain n’a inscrit aucun but sur cette période, mais a délivré une passe décisive en Ligue des champions. Il a également créé 15 occasions de but et affiche une précision de passes comprise entre 90 et 91 %. En championnat de France, le défenseur a participé à six rencontres, totalisant 409 minutes. Il y a créé six occasions, avec un taux de réussite de 91 % dans ses passes, et reçu un carton jaune. En Ligue des champions, il a disputé trois matchs pour 244 minutes de jeu. Il y a délivré une passe décisive et créé sept occasions, avec une précision de passes de 90 %. Hakimi a également participé à une rencontre de la Coupe des champions de France, disputant 90 minutes et créant deux occasions, avec une précision de passes de 92 %. Il a joué 90 minutes supplémentaires en Supercoupe d’Europe, avec un taux de réussite de 87 % dans ses passes. The post Ballon d’Or 2026 : Achraf Hakimi termine à la 13e place appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: KAI poursuit sa campagne auprès des FRA, de Marrakech à Sacheon
items.description: Deux semaines après sa première participation au Marrakech Airshow, le constructeur coréen KAI a ouvert ses chaînes d’assemblage à des représentants marocains, alors que les forces royales air préparent le remplacement de leurs Alpha Jet et de leurs F-5. Le constructeur aéronautique coréen Korea Aerospace Industries (KAI) poursuit sa démarche commerciale auprès des forces royales air (FRA). Vendredi 23 octobre, il a reçu des représentants marocains sur ses chaînes d’assemblage de Sacheon, dans le sud de la Corée, à l’occasion de la « KAI Day », sa journée de prospection internationale. L’enjeu est connu. Les FRA cherchent à renouveler leurs Alpha Jet franco-allemands, en service depuis la fin des années 1970, ainsi que leurs chasseurs légers F-5. KAI défend l’idée qu’une flotte mixte de FA-50 et de T-50 permettrait de remplacer ces deux types d’appareils. Dérivé de l’avion d’entraînement T-50, conçu avec l’américain Lockheed Martin, le FA-50 partage une large part de ses équipements avec le F-16, pilier de l’aviation de combat marocaine. Cet argumentaire avait déjà été déroulé à Marrakech, du 7 au 10 octobre. Seule entreprise coréenne présente au salon, KAI y disposait d’un espace entièrement consacré au FA-50, présenté dans la perspective du programme d’acquisition d’avions d’entraînement avancé engagé par les FRA. Le groupe a insisté sur la double aptitude de l’appareil, capable d’assurer la formation avancée des pilotes comme des missions de combat léger. Son directeur des activités commerciales, Kim Yong-min, y voyait « une occasion idéale » de faire valoir les performances de l’avion et son expérience opérationnelle auprès de clients marocains et africains. Ses équipes ont multiplié, sur place, les entretiens avec des responsables gouvernementaux et militaires du Maroc, du Qatar, des Émirats arabes unis et de l’Arabie saoudite. Un volet industriel a accompagné ce travail de séduction. KAI a signé un protocole d’accord avec deux sociétés marocaines de maintenance aéronautique, Maintenance Aero Maroc et Sabca Maroc, autour d’une coopération liée à une offre de la famille T-50 destinée aux FRA. Les trois entreprises y voient un moyen d’« ouvrir la voie à de nouvelles discussions et à une collaboration potentielle » au profit de l’industrie aéronautique et de défense du royaume. À Sacheon, la délégation marocaine n’était pas la seule invitée. Quatorze pays avaient été conviés, dont les États-Unis, les Philippines, la Pologne, les Émirats arabes unis et la Roumanie, pour quelque quatre-vingts délégués étrangers au total. Ces derniers ont pu examiner en taille réelle le chasseur léger FA-50, le chasseur KF-21 Boramae, l’hélicoptère d’assaut amphibie MAH et l’hélicoptère armé léger LAH. Les drones ont occupé une place de choix dans le programme. KAI a présenté un drone de combat sans pilote (MUCCA), un drone polyvalent (AAP), un drone largué en vol (ALE) et une munition rôdeuse miniature (CMMAV), des appareils dans lesquels le groupe espère trouver de nouveaux débouchés à l’exportation auprès des délégations étrangères. La journée a rassemblé des responsables de l’armée de l’air coréenne et de l’agence des programmes d’acquisition de défense (DAPA), ainsi que des équipes de l’agence pour le développement de la défense (ADD) et de l’agence de technologie et de qualité de défense (DTaQ). Des cadres de l’américain Northrop Grumman, du français Safran et du britannique Rolls-Royce avaient également fait le déplacement. Elle s’est tenue en marge du salon aéronautique de Sacheon, organisé du 22 au 25 octobre par KAI, l’armée de l’air coréenne, la province du Gyeongsang du Sud et la ville de Sacheon. L’édition de cette année accueille une exposition internationale de l’aérospatial et de la défense (GADEX), ouverte à 124 entreprises issues de 22 pays. KAI y a dévoilé son futur système de combat aérien (NACS), qui associe des appareils pilotés et des drones coordonnés par l’intelligence artificielle. The post KAI poursuit sa campagne auprès des FRA, de Marrakech à Sacheon appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Tunisie | Météo : Quel temps pour cette nuit ?
items.description: Au cours de la nuit, le temps sera caractérisé par des passages nuageux sur la plupart des régions, devenant parfois plus abondants en fin de nuit sur l'extrême Sud-est, avec quelques pluies éparses. C'est ce qu'a fait savoir l'Institut National de la Météorologie (INM), en ajoutant que le vent sera relativement fort près des côtes et faible à modéré dans les autres régions, tandis que la mer sera généralement agitée. Pour les températures, l'INM prévoit des nocturnes variant entre 11 et 16 degrés sur les régions ouest du nord et du centre, et entre 17 et 22 degrés ailleurs. items.title: Microsoft offers voluntary exit packages to 60,000 staff
items.description: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, the company said on Monday, roughly a quarter of its workforce, as the tech giant seeks to cut costs while pouring money into artificial intelligence. Staff on select teams in the United States, Canada, India and Britain at vice president level and below will be eligible, a Microsoft spokesperson said, while some groups of employees, including some working on data centres, sales and marketing, are excluded. “The Voluntary Exit Offer reflects an important part of how we’re evolving our approach to change: creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter,” Amy Coleman, an executive vice president and chief people officer, told employees in a memo. It’s the second voluntary buyout offer that Microsoft has offered employees this year. In April, the company reportedly offered around seven per cent of its US workforce the option to retire early. Around 30pc of those eligible took the voluntary retirement plan, according to CNBC . Microsoft had 223,000 employees globally at the end of June, down from 228,000 at the end of 2025, according to regulatory filings. Around 27pc of Microsoft’s workforce is eligible for the new buyout offer. The company is expected to report quarterly earnings later this week. Tech layoffs As major tech giants continue to spend heavily on AI-related investments, concerns persist about the impact of the technology on jobs. Even industry insiders, such as Anthropic Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei, have warned of mass job losses. Netflix will reportedly cut around 6pc of its workforce, or 1,000 jobs, US media reported last week. Auction site eBay laid off 1,000 employees earlier this month, adding to a previous round earlier this year which impacted 800 jobs. In May, Meta laid off around 10pc of its global workforce, impacting around 8,000 employees. In April, Meta also said it would cancel plans to hire an additional 6,000 people and also shift 7,000 other employees into AI workflow-related roles. Ride-hailing giant Uber said in September that it would lay off around 10pc of its staff, impacting an estimated 3,000 or more employees. And e-commerce giant Amazon announced 16,000 global job cuts in January. Microsoft previously cut nearly 5,000 jobs in July that heavily targeted its Xbox gaming division . Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet and Meta are collectively on track to pour roughly $700 billion into AI data centres, chips and computing infrastructure this year alone. In July, Microsoft said it spent $41bn overall between April and June and expected to increase its spending to $50bn between July and September. However, the company also adjusted its forecast for total spending in the 2026 calendar year to $175bn, down from $190bn previously. Around two-thirds of its spending goes towards “short-lived assets,” specifically chips, due to customer demand for “both AI and non-AI infrastructure”, Chief Financial Officer Amy Hood said during a call with analysts.

items.title: Concours national de dissertation : UBA Burkina récompense les huit finalistes
items.description: Du 17 avril au 2 juin 2026, la Fondation UBA a organisé au Burkina Faso le Concours national de dissertation (National Essay Competition, NEC). À l’issue de la finale de cette compétition, organisée sous le thème : « L’école burkinabè face à la transformation digitale : doit-on repenser la stratégie d’éducation nationale ? », les huit finalistes ont reçu leurs prix, ce 23 octobre 2026, des mains de Rasmata Djibo, directrice générale de UBA Burkina. Premier du genre au Burkina Faso, ce concours organisé par la Fondation UBA a reçu au total 1 256 copies, transmises par e-mail et via un formulaire en ligne. Il s’adressait aux élèves des lycées publics ou privés âgés de moins de 18 ans. Une première étape a permis de retenir 760 copies jugées conformes au règlement. Elle a été suivie de la phase finale, qui a concerné huit finalistes. Les trois premiers du concours©️Faso7 Ils ont composé en situation d’examen au siège de UBA Burkina à Ouagadougou et à l’agence principale de Bobo-Dioulasso. Avec une moyenne de 94,625, Tassnim Idrissou, du Prytanée militaire de Kadiogo, s’est imposée à la première place. Elle a reçu un chèque d’un million de FCFA, une moto, un certificat et un sac UBA. Elle est suivie d’Aron Clauvis Yempabou Ouoba, du Lycée scientifique régional de Bobo-Dioulasso, avec 93,7. UBA Burkina lui a offert un chèque de 750 000 FCFA, une moto, un certificat et un sac UBA. La troisième, Estelle Ingrid Tégwendé Nana, du Lycée scientifique national de Ouagadougou, avec 88,325, a reçu un chèque de 500 000 FCFA, une moto, un certificat et un sac. Les cinq autres lauréats repartent chacun avec une moto, un certificat et un sac UBA. « C’est une très grande joie pour moi d’avoir participé à ce concours. Cela m’a permis de me surpasser et de me situer par rapport aux autres candidats. Je remercie vraiment la banque UBA d’avoir pris l’initiative d’organiser ce concours », s’est réjouie Tassnim Idrissou, première du concours. Persuadée que le développement durable de l’Afrique repose sur la qualité de son capital humain, UBA Burkina a initié ce concours. Selon Rasmata Djibo, la directrice générale, les jeunes doivent être dotés de créativité et d’indépendance afin de mettre en place des projets structurants de développement dans leurs pays respectifs. Les huit finalistes©️Faso7 « C’est dans cet esprit que la Fondation UBA porte le Concours national de dissertation et soutient des initiatives éducatives et culturelles telles que Read Africa, qui encourage la lecture et l’accès des jeunes aux livres africains. Un livre peut ouvrir une porte, une idée changer une trajectoire et une éducation de qualité transformer une société », a expliqué Rasmata Djibo. Tout en félicitant les lauréats, elle les a invités à persévérer dans leurs apprentissages et à mettre leur savoir au service de la nation. Elle a invité l’ensemble des élèves à s’inscrire dans cette dynamique, car ils ont aussi leur part à accomplir dans le processus de développement. Cheick Habib Désiré BAYILI Faso7 L’article Concours national de dissertation : UBA Burkina récompense les huit finalistes est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: From Nigeria to Multiple Markets Across Borders: How SharpPunter Is Changing the Way Punters Analyse Sports
items.description: A typical Saturday slip in Nigeria is put together from several places at once: a booking code a tipster posted in a WhatsApp group with no explanation behind it, a few games a friend swore were safe, and, for many fans, their own club, added out of loyalty before anyone has checked its form. If the code was shared from a bookmaker the punter does not use, he first has to rebuild it on his own bookmaker by hand, one match at a time, and once it is placed, a single one of its twelve games going the wrong way is enough to take down the slip and every version of it shared around the group, a pattern that repeats with codes passed around in Accra, Nairobi and Douala. SharpPunter, a sports analysis platform built in Nigeria, was set up to give those punters a clearer look at what they are betting on before they place the slip. Six months after its launch in April 2026, it has users across West, East and Southern Africa, works with booking codes from 37 bookmakers and has just released V2, a rebuilt version of its app. Built in Nigeria, for the way Nigerians bet “I built SharpPunter because I was tired of seeing people stake their money on tips they had not checked by themselves, and I wanted something that would help punters truly understand which games were worth backing,” said Oluwatobi Abobade, who founded SharpPunter. “Over time, the way people use the product has shaped how we built V2. Users kept tagging our X bot with codes from friends, so checking a code is now one of the two things you see when you open the app. We also saw how closely people follow their own clubs and how often that turns their picks into emotional ones, so V2 lets you follow your club, get updates on its live matches and see the stats, alongside unbiased picks you can use.” Where slips go wrong, and what SharpPunter does about it The first problem is the tip itself, since most codes that circulate in group chats arrive with no rationale, and give punters no way to judge whether the picks are valid. Every SharpPunter pick shows the reasoning behind it, such as a team’s recent form or its record against that opponent, and carries a rating of Strong, Fair or Slim, and the Optimizer reads any code a user pastes in and rates each match SharpPunter covers. The second is the single weak game that usually sinks a whole accumulator, often across every variation of the slip a punter has placed. In V2, the Optimizer flags the weakest selections on a code and suggests swaps before the bet goes in, while the Shuffle tool deals the matches from several codes into balanced slips so that one bad pick cannot take all of them down. The third is the code that only works on one bookmaker, which leaves punters rebuilding a friend’s slip by hand, one match at a time. SharpPunter’s converter rebuilds the same matches on the punter’s own bookmaker, and it now supports conversions across 37 bookmakers. On top of these, many fans let loyalty make the call and back their own club out of habit. SharpPunter’s model has no favourite team, so its picks show how a game rates on the numbers whichever team a fan supports, and in V2 users can also follow a club to get updates on its matches as they happen, with club pages showing its recent results, its next fixture and the league table. V2 also adds a Live tab that lets users monitor games in real time, with the score, goalscorers, possession, shots, expected goals and corners updating during the match, and a rebuilt SharpSlips that puts together a slip based on how many picks a user wants and how adventurous they want it to be. Hot on X and the new Community tab The newest part of V2 is a Community tab, built around the booking codes people already share. Its Hot on X feed gathers codes posted by popular accounts on X into one place, so a user does not have to scroll through timelines to find them. Codes can be filtered by bookmaker and sorted by what is hot, newest, most viewed, or starting soon, and each one shows the number of picks, the total odds, the kick-off time, and how many SharpPunter users have checked it. From the feed, a user can copy a code to their own bookmaker or run it through the Optimizer to see how SharpPunter rates each selection before deciding whether to play it. The tab also has a Trending feed, which shows the matches most looked at on SharpPunter over the last 24 hours and which way the crowd is leaning on each one, and a Following feed, where users can keep up with the codes checked and converted by the people they follow. Weekly tasks in the tab, such as checking a code or booking a slip, earn credits for the booking code tools. Demand from outside Nigeria came within weeks SharpPunter’s first users were in Nigeria and Ghana, and the early product followed the way they already played, with accumulators, booking codes and slips passed around on X, Telegram and WhatsApp. SharpSlips, the platform’s slip builder, put together accumulators from the day’s strongest picks, while the Shuffle tool and an X bot, @SharpPunterAI, which reviewed any booking code a user tagged it in, gave users ways to work with the slips they already had. SharpPunter was designed with West Africa in mind, but within weeks of launch, sign-ups were coming in from Kenya, South Africa and other parts of East and Southern Africa, as well as from Africans living abroad. The platform now sells its plans in local currency in Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa, Zambia, Uganda, Tanzania and Rwanda, and in CFA francs for users in francophone West and Central Africa, including Cameroon, Senegal and Côte d’Ivoire, with prices also listed in US dollars. “We built SharpPunter in Nigeria, but the slip that dies on one bad game looks the same in Accra, Nairobi and Johannesburg,” Abobade said. “If we can show a punter which game is carrying the risk before they play, we have done our job, and sometimes that means telling them the slip is not worth playing at all.” One converter for 37 bookmakers SharpPunter’s booking code converter takes a code, reads the selections directly from the bookmaker it came from, and rebuilds the same matches as a new code on the user’s own bookmaker, naming any selection the new bookmaker does not offer so that nothing goes missing without the user knowing. The supported bookmakers include SportyBet, Bet9ja, Football.com, MSport, Betika, 1xBet, 22Bet, BetWinner, Melbet, PariPesa and Helabet, and a user can paste any code to see every match on it for free before deciding whether to convert it. What comes next SharpPunter’s rebuilt app is free to start on iOS, Android and sharppunter.com , and first-time users get full access to its premium features for a limited period, so they can try everything before choosing a plan. After that, users can subscribe to unlock every prediction, or buy credits if they only want the booking code tools. None of it changes what happens on the pitch, but a punter who checks SharpPunter before placing a slip can now see the reasoning behind each game, which selections are weakest, and how every match rates on the numbers, including the ones involving the team they support. About SharpPunter SharpPunter is an AI-assisted sports analysis platform covering football (soccer), basketball and tennis, with volleyball and American football planned next. Launched in Nigeria in April 2026, it publishes daily predictions with the reasoning behind each pick, settles every pick publicly against the final result, and offers tools to check, optimise, convert, merge and shuffle booking codes across 37 bookmakers. Sports fans across West, East and Southern Africa can sign up at sharppunter.com or on iOS and Android and pay for a plan in their own local currency. SharpPunter provides sports analysis and predictions for information only. It is not a bookmaker and does not accept or settle bets. No prediction is guaranteed, and past results do not promise future outcomes. Betting is for people aged 18 and over. Only stake what you can afford to lose, and seek support from a responsible gambling organisation if betting stops being fun. The post From Nigeria to Multiple Markets Across Borders: How SharpPunter Is Changing the Way Punters Analyse Sports appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Octobre rose : la JCI Ouaga Golden mobilise contre les cancers féminins
items.description: La Jeune Chambre internationale (JCI) Ouaga Golden, en partenariat avec la Fondation Bank of Africa (BOA), organise du 26 au 28 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou une campagne de sensibilisation et de dépistage gratuit des cancers du sein et du col de l’utérus. Cette initiative s’inscrit dans le cadre d’Octobre rose. Placée sous le thème « Parce qu’elle compte : dépistons tôt, accompagnons mieux » , cette 12e édition a été officiellement lancée le lundi 26 octobre 2026 à l’agence BOA de Kossodo. Elle est portée avec la Fondation BOA et l’Association burkinabè des sages-femmes et maïeuticiens. L’initiative vise à renforcer l’information sur les cancers féminins, à combattre les idées reçues et à encourager le dépistage précoce. Les séances se déroulent de 8 h à 16 h sur trois sites : l’agence BOA de Kossodo, la clinique de sages-femmes de Paspanga et le CSPS de Nongtaba. Prévention et accompagnement au cœur de cette édition Cette édition, selon Sylvère Kaboré, vice-président exécutif de la JCI Golden pour l’année 2026, représentant le président, met davantage l’accent sur la vaccination des jeunes filles et le suivi des femmes dépistées. « Notre objectif reste le même : sensibiliser, dépister, vacciner et accompagner. Cette année, nous voulons renforcer la prévention dès le bas âge et faciliter l’orientation des femmes vers les services compétents pour le suivi de leurs cas. Nous souhaitons ainsi apporter notre contribution à la lutte contre ces maladies, avec des approches innovantes » , a-t-il expliqué. Les organisateurs ambitionnent de dépister entre 500 et 1 000 femmes à Ouagadougou, de vacciner 250 jeunes filles et de sensibiliser près de 5 000 femmes grâce aux actions de communication digitale. Cet engagement, pour Nathalie Sawadogo Traoré, représentante de la Fondation BOA, repose sur la nécessité de faire de la prévention une responsabilité collective. « La santé est l’affaire de tous. Être en bonne santé nous permet de travailler et de mener nos activités. Le dépistage favorise une détection précoce et une meilleure prise en charge » , a-t-elle souligné. La marraine de cette édition, Stéphanie Sanou, a également invité les femmes à se faire dépister précocement. Elle a insisté sur l’importance de la prévention pour favoriser une meilleure prise en charge. « Aucune femme ne devrait avoir honte de se faire dépister. Aucune femme ne devrait être jugée parce qu’elle est malade. Aucune femme ne devrait être abandonnée au moment où elle a le plus besoin de soutien » , a-t-elle confié. Des partenaires honorés, un hommage rendu à Paule Christelle Ouédraogo/Sanou La cérémonie officielle a réuni les responsables de la JCI, les partenaires, les professionnels de santé et plusieurs invités. Elle a été marquée par des allocutions et la remise de trophées de reconnaissance et d’honneur aux partenaires, en hommage à leur engagement aux côtés de l’organisation. Un hommage particulier a été rendu à Paule Christelle Ouédraogo/Sanou, qui a contribué au développement du projet pendant plus d’une décennie. Elle est décédée au cours de la préparation de cette édition. Lancée depuis le 20 octobre 2026, la mobilisation se poursuivra jusqu’au 31 octobre avec une séance d’aérobic. À travers ces différentes activités, la JCI Ouaga Golden entend renforcer la sensibilisation et encourager davantage de femmes à participer aux actions de prévention. Éléonore Savadogo Faso7 L’article Octobre rose : la JCI Ouaga Golden mobilise contre les cancers féminins est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Ghana’s road deaths demand urgent action, researchers warn
items.description: Researchers Enock Aninakwah and Isaac Aninakwah are calling for coordinated action to reduce road deaths in Ghana, citing unsafe road conditions, dangerous driving, and weaknesses in enforcement. In a paper titled A Nation in Motion, A People in Mourning: A Lamentation on Ghana’s Road Carnage, the authors argue that the country needs sustained improvements in road infrastructure, vehicle safety and emergency response. The paper examines road traffic fatalities between 1991 and 2024 using existing records and published research. It cites more than 46,000 deaths between 1991 and 2018, alongside reported figures of 2,494 deaths and 15,607 injuries in 2024. The authors say the consequences extend beyond those killed or injured. Families also face lost income, the cost of caring for survivors and emotional distress. “The findings of this study show that Ghana’s road safety crisis is driven by a chain of interconnected systemic failures rather than isolated factors,” they write. Enock Aninakwah is affiliated with the University of Ghana’s Department of Geography and Resource Development, while Isaac Aninakwah is affiliated with the Department of Social Sciences at St. Monica’s College of Education in Mampong. Their analysis draws on sources including the National Road Safety Authority, the Ghana Highway Authority, the World Health Organisation and earlier studies. The paper identifies poor road design and maintenance, inadequate lighting and signage, risky overtaking and unsafe vehicles among the concerns requiring attention. It argues that these problems are compounded by weak enforcement and gaps in emergency response, making a coordinated approach necessary. The researchers recommend safer road design, appropriate separation of opposing traffic, improved road maintenance and stronger vehicle roadworthiness checks. They also call for sustained public education, enforcement against dangerous driving and better coordination among institutions responsible for transport and public safety. Drawing on earlier research, the authors describe fear and anxiety surrounding everyday travel, warning that repeated fatal crashes can weaken public confidence in the transport system. They urge authorities to treat road safety as a public health and development priority and use reliable data to monitor whether interventions are reducing deaths and injuries. The analysis relies mainly on reported fatality counts. The authors acknowledge that consistent long-term information on vehicle use and distances travelled was unavailable, limiting their ability to assess changes in risk relative to road use. Read the full paper attached below. A NATION IN MOTION, A PEOPLE IN MOUNING Download

items.title: PLFR 2026 : l’Assemblée nationale ouverte à une solution consensuelle avec le Gouvernement
items.description: L’Assemblée nationale se dit disposée à rencontrer le Gouvernement, dès cet après-midi, pour poursuivre les échanges autour de l’examen du projet de loi de finances rectificative (PLFR) pour l’année 2026. Dans une note d’information publiée ce lundi 26 octobre, l’institution parlementaire réaffirme sa disponibilité au dialogue, tout en précisant les conditions d’une concertation susceptible de déboucher sur un compromis. Cette ouverture intervient à la suite d’une demande du Premier ministre visant à poursuivre les échanges avec les autorités parlementaires autour de l’examen du PLFR 2026. Dans sa note, l’Assemblée nationale précise que le président de la Commission des Finances et du Contrôle budgétaire a saisi, ce lundi, le ministre de l’Économie, des Finances et du Budget afin d’obtenir des informations et des documents complémentaires sur le projet de loi. L’institution parlementaire estime que cette démarche est nécessaire pour permettre une discussion utile et constructive sur les points demeurés en suspens. Elle rappelle, par ailleurs, que l’examen du texte relève prioritairement de la Commission des Finances et du Contrôle budgétaire ainsi que des groupes parlementaires. Selon la note, le président de l’Assemblée nationale ne participe ni aux travaux des commissions ni aux débats en séance plénière. Sur le plan procédural, l’Assemblée nationale souligne que les travaux de la commission étant clos et la séance plénière étant prévue ce mardi 27 octobre, aucune nouvelle procédure formelle ne peut raisonnablement être engagée avant l’examen du texte en plénière. Malgré cette contrainte, l’institution se dit prête à recevoir le Gouvernement, selon une composition à sa convenance, pouvant comprendre le Premier ministre, le ministre chargé des Finances et les autres ministres concernés. « Notre disponibilité au dialogue est entière », affirme l’Assemblée nationale, qui dit vouloir rechercher un compromis dans le respect des prérogatives de chaque institution et sur la base de réponses précises aux préoccupations soulevées par les parlementaires. L’institution parlementaire place ainsi l’intérêt supérieur du peuple sénégalais au cœur de sa démarche, à la veille de l’examen du PLFR 2026 en séance plénière. S.G

items.title: Playback: JoyNews Research fact-checks South Africa evacuation cost claims
items.description: When hundreds of Ghanaians needed help returning home from South Africa, the government stepped in to facilitate their evacuation. But questions have since emerged over how public funds were spent and whether the records submitted by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs accurately reflect the payments made. Now, a JoyNews Research investigation has uncovered what appear to be forged signatures and discrepancies in payment records contained in the Ministry’s data. Who received the money? Do the records accurately account for the expenditure? And how did documents with questionable signatures become part of the data used to account for a government-funded operation? As the controversy deepens and demands for accountability grow, JoyNews examines the documents, traces the inconsistencies and investigates the questions surrounding the evacuation exercise. This is a closer look at the South Africa evacuation controversy – and the troubling gaps between the records and the money they are supposed to account for. Watch the livestream here:

items.title: Robles advierte en la ONU de que la paz no puede construirse de espaldas a las mujeres
items.description: La ministra de Defensa, Margarita Robles , ha subrayado este lunes en Naciones Unidas el papel de la mujer en la resolución de los conflictos y ha advertido de que “la paz no puede construirse de espaldas a la mitad de la humanidad”. Robles, que ha participado en el encuentro de alto nivel sobre mujeres, paz y seguridad celebrado en Nueva York, ha planteado un objetivo mínimo del 5% de participación femenina en las Fuerzas Armadas y por encima del 15% para los países “que ya cuentan con una presencia apreciable de mujeres” en sus ejércitos ( en España representan el 13,4% ). Además, ha pedido aumentar hasta un porcentaje de entre el 13% y el 15% su participación en misiones militares de la ONU —las mujeres suponen el 10.6% de los contingentes españoles en el exterior— y crear, como estímulo, un distintivo o reconocimiento para las militares que acumulen tiempo de servicio en operaciones de paz. items.title: Govt raises petrol price by Rs1.54 per litre, high-speed diesel rate by Rs2.16
items.description: The government on Monday increased the price of petrol by Rs1.54 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.16. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs379.25 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs395.82 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 27 (Tuesday). On Friday, the Pakistan Petroleum Dealers Association had urged consumers not to resort to panic buying, as excessive purchases could create market distortions. The same day, senators raised concerns over fuel supply even after Minister of State for Finance and Revenue Bilal Azhar Kayani said that there were no supply issues. PPP’s Sherry Rehman questioned petrol availability for December and Opposition Leader Raja Nasir Abbas warned of a bleak situation amid heightening Middle East tensions. The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50 per cent for three months. On Sept 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: Après son opération d’un cancer du poumon, Léon XIV maintient sa tournée sud-américaine
items.description: Le pape Léon XIV effectuera bien sa tournée apostolique en Uruguay, en Argentine et au Pérou, du 6 au 17 novembre 2026. Le Vatican a confirmé, le lundi 26 octobre, le maintien de ce déplacement, après son opération du poumon droit subie par le souverain pontife le 13 octobre dernier à Rome. Selon le Vatican, son équipe médicale ne relève aucune contre-indication à ce voyage. Les interrogations sur la capacité du pape à honorer son programme en Amérique du Sud sont ainsi levées. Âgé de 71 ans, Léon XIV a subi, à l’hôpital Gemelli de Rome, l’ablation du lobe inférieur de son poumon droit, touché par un adénocarcinome pulmonaire. Selon les résultats médicaux communiqués par le Saint-Siège, la tumeur était localisée et aucun traitement oncologique supplémentaire n’est nécessaire. Le rétablissement du souverain pontife évolue favorablement. Après sa sortie de l’hôpital, il a progressivement repris ses activités au Vatican, tout en poursuivant sa convalescence sous surveillance médicale. Un périple de douze jours attend désormais le chef de l’Église catholique. Au départ de Montevideo, en Uruguay, il poursuivra son déplacement en Argentine, puis au Pérou. Le programme prévoit environ 31 000 kilomètres de trajet, une douzaine de vols, ainsi que plusieurs dizaines de prises de parole. L’altitude de certaines étapes péruviennes constitue notamment un défi supplémentaire pour ce voyage particulièrement dense. Au-delà de son importance pastorale, cette tournée revêt une dimension personnelle pour Léon XIV, qui a passé de nombreuses années au Pérou. Elle doit lui permettre de rencontrer les communautés catholiques et de porter un message de foi, d’espérance et de paix. Le maintien de ce déplacement marque ainsi une nouvelle étape dans la reprise progressive des activités pontificales après l’intervention chirurgicale. Le pape devra toutefois concilier les exigences de son agenda international avec les précautions nécessaires à la poursuite de sa convalescence. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Après son opération d’un cancer du poumon, Léon XIV maintient sa tournée sud-américaine est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: EKUMFI: How $6M EXIM participation built a $53M industrial asset — Now poised for a 24-Hour economy breakthrough
items.description: With the 20% excise duty on local fruit juices now abolished, the government’s Feed the Industries Programme offers Ekumfi Fruits & Juices a pathway to US$48 million in annual turnover, more than 9,000 acres of fruit cultivation, and up to GH₵52,000 in gross revenue per acre for youth and farmers growing pineapple. The transformation could also open a route to accelerated EXIM debt repayment. Ghana’s industrialization journey may be entering a defining chapter. Ekumfi Fruits & Juices Limited is emerging as a potential model for turning development-finance investment into agricultural prosperity, youth employment, industrial expansion, and export growth. With approximately US$6 million in Ghana EXIM Bank participation, Ekumfi has built an industrial enterprise with an estimated asset value of US$53 million — a modern fruit-processing facility, Ghanaian juice brands, and a foundation for international market expansion. Yet this substantial investment has lived with a contradiction. Despite significant processing capacity, the company has been constrained by inadequate supplies of pineapple and other fruits, and by the 20% excise duty imposed on locally manufactured fruit juices in 2023. At times, production has been limited to roughly two days a week, leaving equipment and infrastructure underused. The cost reaches well beyond the company. Farmers lose an established industrial buyer. Young people miss employment and enterprise opportunities. Ghana loses manufacturing output and export earnings. Ekumfi’s challenge has never simply been the existence of a factory. It has been building the agricultural and financial ecosystem needed to keep that factory running at its potential. Today, the government’s excise reforms, the Feed the Industries Programme and the 24-Hour Economy agenda create an opening to address those structural constraints. The Excise Duty Removal Creates a New Opening Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson announced the abolition of the 20% excise duty on locally manufactured fruit juices in the 2026 Mid-Year Budget Review on 23 July. The exemption, enacted under the Excise Duty Act, 2026, took effect on 1 October 2026. For Ekumfi, the change can improve price competitiveness, strengthen operating margins, stimulate consumer demand and free up room for reinvestment in agricultural production. But removing the tax solves only one side of the industrial equation. The more fundamental challenge is raw material. A processing plant cannot run three shifts a day when its agricultural supply chain supports only a fraction of installed capacity. This is where Feed the Industries becomes decisive. Feed the Industries: Linking Ghana’s Farms to Its Factories The Feed the Industries Programme, under the 24-Hour Economy framework, is designed to connect agricultural production directly to industrial demand. For Ekumfi, that means a coordinated fruit-supply system drawing on commercial estates, smallholder farmers, youth agricultural enterprises, outgrower cooperatives and agricultural service providers. Management estimates that sustained 24-hour operations would require more than 9,000 acres of pineapple and other fruits. Crucially, the land is already in place. Ekumfi has secured 9,500 acres for juice, tea and tepache feedstock — more than the full 24-hour requirement — with full capacity achievable within 36 months. The constraint is no longer land, but the planting finance, inputs and grower mobilization needed to bring it into production. That is not merely an agricultural challenge. It is a major economic opportunity. Rather than relying solely on company-owned plantations, Ekumfi can establish structured partnerships with thousands of farmers and young entrepreneurs growing fruit under agreed quality, delivery and pricing terms. The factory gains dependable supply; growers gain a defined industrial market. Feed the Industries can turn Ekumfi’s raw-material shortage into rural wealth creation. GH₵52,000 Per Acre: A New Opportunity for Youth and Pineapple Growers The most compelling dimension of the proposed expansion is the opening it creates for youth, smallholders, landowners, and agricultural entrepreneurs to participate directly in the pineapple value chain. Under the proposed cultivation model, one acre of pineapple could generate an estimated GH₵52,000 in gross revenue per successful harvest cycle . Young people could start commercial farming on modest plots; existing growers could scale up. THE EKUMFI PINEAPPLE GROWER OPPORTUNITY: GH₵52,000 Potential gross revenue per acre per harvest cycle; 9,000+ Acres of pineapple and other fruits potentially required; 9,500 Acres of land already secured Farm size Potential gross crop revenue 1 acreGH₵52,0005 acresGH₵260,00010 acresGH₵520,000100 acresGH₵5.2 million1,000 acresGH₵52 million9,000 acresGH₵468 million Illustrative estimates assuming all acreage is planted with pineapple and each acre achieves GH₵52,000 gross revenue per harvest. Actual earnings depend on yields, prices, crop cycles, and production costs. If the full 9,000-acre requirement were planted with pineapple at this revenue level, gross farm-gate value could reach GH₵468 million per harvest cycle. Because Ekumfi also needs other fruits, the real mix will depend on acreage allocated to each crop. The programme could be structured around one-acre, five-acre and ten-acre production units for young growers, backed by land access, improved planting material, technical assistance, mechanization and structured offtake agreements. The opportunity extends well beyond the farm gate: seedling multiplication, land preparation, irrigation, harvesting, transport, aggregation, farm management and agricultural technology could each support thousands of livelihoods. Management estimates that the full Ekumfi value chain — nurseries, land preparation, cultivation, harvesting, haulage, aggregation, processing, packaging and distribution — could support around 18,000 jobs in the Central Region alone . One distinction matters. GH₵52,000 is potential gross revenue , not guaranteed profit. Growers must cover cultivation, labour, inputs, financing and transport, and a pineapple cycle can run longer than a year. Even so, the model shows how industrial demand can anchor commercial agriculture. Instead of simply urging young Ghanaians into farming, the country can offer them a defined industrial market, structured production support and a real pathway to commercial income. From Two Days a Week to US$4 Million a Month Management estimates that with adequate raw material, working capital and market access, sustained 24-hour production could deliver monthly turnover of about US$4 million — US$48 million a year . EKUMFI’S PROPOSED INDUSTRIAL TRANSFORMATION US$53M Estimated industrial asset value US$4M Projected monthly turnover US$48M Projected annual turnover 24 HRS Target operations 18,000 Value-chain jobs, Central Region Company-supplied projections, subject to commercial, financial and operational validation. Moving from two days a week toward continuous operation would sharply improve utilization of existing equipment, utilities, labour and infrastructure, while expanding market presence and multiplying demand for local produce. The lesson for Ghana’s industrial agenda is clear: the country can unlock substantial value not only by building new factories, but by helping existing ones run at full capacity. Could Ekumfi Repay Its EXIM Debt Within One Year? One of the most consequential implications concerns Ekumfi’s obligations to Ghana EXIM Bank. At US$48 million in annual turnover, the company would generate materially stronger cash flow to support restructuring and repayment. Illustratively, a 15% free-cash-flow margin would yield about US$7.2 million before further financing needs or restrictions on distributions. At that level, a US$6 million obligation could theoretically be cleared within 12 months, provided sufficient cash were dedicated to debt service. The actual timeline will depend on the verified outstanding balance, accrued interest, operating margins, working-capital needs and agreed repayment terms. The original US$6 million participation should not be confused with the current outstanding debt, which may differ substantially. The broader point stands: restoring industrial productivity offers development financiers a more credible recovery pathway than leaving major manufacturing assets idle. A structured recovery programme can align EXIM’s repayment interests with agricultural expansion, higher factory output and growing export revenue. From Ghanaian Pineapples to a Global Juice Brand Ekumfi’s processing platform can produce value-added beverages from pineapple, citrus, ginger, passion fruit and other local crops. With adequate volumes, competitive pricing, consistent quality and established distribution partners, the company can extend its reach across African, European, North American and Middle Eastern markets. The gains ripple through the economy: more fruit production creates farm income; more manufacturing creates industrial jobs; packaging and distribution support other businesses; exports earn foreign exchange. This is the central promise of agricultural industrialization — converting locally grown crops into internationally marketed finished products, and capturing value through processing, branding and distribution rather than exporting raw produce. Why Ekumfi Survived Where State-Led Factories Stalled Ekumfi’s story becomes sharper when set beside the record of state-led agro-industrial investment in the same region and beyond. The Komenda Sugar Factory in the Central Region was first established in 1964 and shut down in the early 1990s. It was rebuilt and recommissioned in 2016 with about US$35 million in Indian government-backed financing, yet it has remained largely dormant. In February 2026, the trade minister told Parliament the factory had been disconnected from power and water over unpaid bills, with its machinery not refurbished since 2016. Government now targets a revival by the end of 2026. The state-owned Ayensu Starch Company , set up in 2002 to process cassava in the Central Region, has shut down repeatedly over raw-material and fuel shortages and equipment breakdowns, leaving cassava farmers without a dependable buyer. Napcoas followed a similar path: public commitment without sustained private ownership to carry it through. Under One District, One Factory (1D1F) , more than 300 factories were left at various stages of completion after the programme was cancelled in 2025, and several that did open struggled to secure raw materials or working capital. The common thread is not a shortage of public money. Over three decades and more, the state has committed capital to factories without the sustained private ownership, management discipline and equity at risk needed to keep them running when conditions turned difficult. Ekumfi took a different route. Backed by private sponsors with their own capital committed, it has kept its factory, brands and markets alive through the excise burden, raw-material shortfalls and financing delays — and today sells Ghanaian juice at home and abroad. That is a lesson the state should note. Rather than building and running factories on its own, or simply recovering legacy debt from the private ventures that survived, government and its development finance institutions should consider taking equity positions alongside committed private sponsors . Equity aligns the state with the upside as utilization rises, strengthens the balance sheet lenders look to, and leaves day-to-day management with operators who have proven they can keep a factory running. Ekumfi offers a ready test case. A Practical Model for the 24-Hour Economy Ekumfi can serve as a demonstration project for how Feed the Industries and the 24-Hour Economy work together. The model connects six elements: Agricultural expansion — develop 9,000+ acres of pineapple and other fruits through company estates, commercial growers and outgrower arrangements. Youth and farmer empowerment — enable growers to target gross crop revenue of up to GH₵52,000 per acre per successful harvest cycle. Industrial production — progressively raise factory utilizations toward sustained 24-hour operation. Market development — expand domestic distribution and exports to support projected turnover of US$48 million a year. Financial recovery — restructure existing obligations and tie debt repayment to actual operating cash flow. State equity partnership — convert public support into equity alongside private sponsors, sharing in the upside of a working factory rather than funding stalled ones. Delivery requires collaboration among Ekumfi, Ghana EXIM Bank, the Ministry of Food and Agriculture, the Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, the 24-Hour Economy Authority, agricultural investors and commercial financiers — and a phased implementation plan with independently validated yields, acreage, processing capacity, customer demand and working-capital needs. The Bigger Picture: Turning Industrial Investment into National Wealth Ekumfi’s story poses a question for Ghana’s development-finance strategy: what happens when the country invests in a major industrial asset but not in the supply chain needed to sustain it? The answer is an underused factory, mounting financial pressure, lost farm income and missed exports. The reverse is just as true. When agriculture, manufacturing, finance and markets are coordinated, the same investment becomes an engine of growth. For young people, the opportunity can begin with a single acre of pineapple. For established farmers, it means scaling up with a dependable industrial buyer. For Ghana EXIM Bank, it offers a pathway to improved recovery through higher production. For Ghana, it demonstrates how Feed the Industries can turn agricultural potential into manufacturing output, export earnings and rural prosperity. The Ekumfi Opportunity Is Bigger Than One Factory The abolition of the 20% excise duty has resolved a key competitiveness problem. Feed the Industries offers a framework for tackling the raw-material constraint. The 24-Hour Economy agenda supplies the wider ambition. What remains is coordinated execution. Ghana does not need to abandon valuable industrial investments because they have faced difficulty. It needs to identify and remove the constraints holding them back. For Ekumfi Fruits & Juices, that means connecting a modern processing factory to thousands of acres of productive farmland, empowering young growers and expanding markets for Ghanaian-made beverages — moving from limited weekly runs to 24-hour operation, from raw-material shortage to a structured supply chain, and from financial pressure to a firm foundation for repayment and export growth. The factory has been built. The asset exists. The land has been acquired. The task now is to feed the factory, empower the farmers, create wealth for the youth and build a globally competitive Ghanaian juice brand. That is the promise of Ekumfi under Ghana’s Feed the Industries and 24-Hour Economy agenda. Editorial note: Financial, acreage and grower-income figures are management estimates and illustrative projections. The US$53 million asset valuation, projected US$48 million annual turnover, GH₵52,000 gross revenue per acre and proposed debt-repayment timetable require independent validation. The GH₵468 million farm-gate estimate assumes all 9,000 acres are planted with pineapple and should not be read as annual profit or guaranteed farmer income.
